entries.statement: A release MUST be built and verified against one declared standards profile, and every part of it MUST use that same profile: authoring, compiler validation, compiled artifacts, runtime evaluation, interchange, diagnostics, and generated compatibility data.

A release MUST NOT resolve any part of the profile from an unpinned latest revision at build time or at run time, and MUST NOT infer an edition from a package label or from the host runtime's own data.
A release MUST be built and verified against Unicode 17.0.0 and Unicode CLDR and LDML 48.2.
A release MUST derive every such table from a source recorded under section 4, and MUST NOT ship a source package's data wholesale.

An Equator release MUST canonicalize a locale identity from the pinned CLDR release and the recorded IANA Language Subtag Registry snapshot, and MUST NOT let a host runtime's own registry decide an identity that is stored, compared, or exchanged.
Script and region distinctions are decided categorically elsewhere in this profile and MUST NOT be reopened as distances.

An Equator release MUST record every source it derives data from, or verifies conformance against, in `standards/sources.lock.json`, with the exact release, the acquisition URL, the role, the license, and a digest.
A vendored source MUST match its recorded digest byte for byte.

A source that is not vendored MUST record the digest of the artifact that was acquired, and where that artifact is an installed package, that digest MUST be the one the package manager recorded for the same version.
A vendored source MUST carry beside it the notice its license requires on copies, recorded in the lock with its digest, or the lock MUST record why its license requires none.
Every file under `standards/data/` MUST belong to a recorded source as its data or its notice.

A release MUST use the host's ECMA-402 implementation as its locale-data and formatting engine, and MUST: - invoke every capability with an explicit locale and explicit options; - feature-detect a capability before relying on it; - return a typed unsupported outcome where a required capability is absent, rather than a substitute result; - treat host locale data as presentation only, never as an identity, a protocol value, or a cache key.
A release MUST NOT carry a second formatting implementation or a locale database that duplicates what the host supplies.
Where a host capability is materially inconsistent with the standard it implements, a release MAY replace that one answer from a locked source, or MAY declare the combination unsupported.
entries.reason: This grants two ways of handling a faulty host answer and requires neither, so no behavior of a release can break it. What must not happen when neither is taken is statement 13.

entries.statement: It MUST NOT let a known inconsistency reach a rendered result.
Correctness-bearing localization behavior MUST NOT vary between supported toolkit, server, and browser combinations.
Server-rendered output that participates in hydration MUST produce the same initial localized result in the browser.
Two independently rendered environments MAY differ cosmetically where meaning, information, safety, accessibility, and identity are unchanged and no hydration comparison is involved.
entries.reason: This permits a cosmetic difference between environments and obliges nothing, so no release behavior can violate it.

entries.statement: Formatted presentation text MUST NOT become an identity, a protocol field, a persisted domain value, or a cache key.
A release MUST be verified against the working group's conformance suite for that same edition, run through the built packages rather than through their sources.
Draft material from a later LDML edition MUST NOT enter the profile except by moving the whole profile to that edition.
A release MUST NOT accept an option it does not read: the message would render without it and report nothing.
A release MUST reject an unknown, unimplemented, or incompatible function rather than guess at it, and MUST NOT rename a draft standard function to hide its status.
A domain that stores the same rate as `25` declares that scale explicitly through the typed formatting profile, and a release MUST NOT infer a scale from a value's magnitude.
Percentage points are a separate contract and MUST NOT enter `:percent` implicitly; `08-formatting-parsing-and-domain.spec.md` states how a declared scale is preserved and reversed.
A release MUST NOT present this profile as implemented until all ten functions and their option vocabularies are implemented and verified.
entries.reason: This governs what a release says about itself in its documentation and release notes, which no program reads. The implementation it depends on is proven by the conformance stage (statement 18) and the option checks (statements 20 and 21).

entries.statement: A release MAY accept explicitly registered custom MessageFormat functions.
entries.reason: This permits custom functions and requires nothing, so no release behavior can violate it.

entries.statement: Standard functions remain preferred, and an extension MUST name its functions in a namespace its provider owns so that one cannot collide with Unicode's or with another extension's.
A custom function has two projections, and a release MUST keep them separate.
The toolkit MUST read a descriptor as data and MUST NOT import or execute an application module to discover one.
A missing or mismatched descriptor or handler MUST fail compilation, generation, or artifact admission before any message is evaluated.
A catalog MAY reference a registered function and MUST NOT carry, fetch, discover, or execute its code.
An extension's handler MUST be deterministic, synchronous, bounded, and safe under server rendering.
It MUST NOT perform network or filesystem access, DOM work, dependency injection, asynchronous acquisition, global mutation, or environment-dependent selection while a message is being evaluated.
entries.reason: This binds the extension author. What a handler does inside its own call cannot be intercepted by the runtime that calls it; the one consequence the runtime can see, a result that is still pending, is the synchronous rule under statement 31.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT emit or accept XLIFF 2.1 by default.

Support for it MAY be added as an explicitly versioned adapter for a workflow whose tooling cannot read the normative profile, and an older tool's limitation MUST NOT silently downgrade what the toolkit writes.
A release MUST NOT treat it as an authoring format, as a runtime format, or as a source of message identity.
XLIFF processing MUST NOT execute document content or fetch a schema, DTD, entity, key, or any other external resource.
A document a release writes MUST validate against the schemas of the pinned Committee Specification.
Content belonging to another official module, or to another vendor's extension, MUST NOT be removed, flattened, or treated as understood.

The mapping MUST preserve: - complete provider, scope, and message identity; - source and target locales; - the source fingerprint and the revision relationship; - MessageFormat declarations, selectors, variants, variables, functions, and options; - typed inputs and catalog-visible contracts; - rich-slot and inline-code identity; - notes, context, and segment state.

A release MUST read back only its own categories: a note written by a translator or by a translation-management system is reported and left in the document rather than absorbed into a catalog, and source guidance that returns changed is reported rather than applied.
A note MUST NOT be removed silently.
A segment in the initial state MUST NOT be imported as a translation, because an initial target is a placeholder rather than translated work.
A state the standard does not define MUST fail the import.

A translator MAY reorder human-language content and protected placeholders as far as the message contract allows, and MUST NOT alter protected identity, introduce executable behavior, or remove required structure.
An import that cannot reconstruct equivalent semantics MUST fail with an actionable diagnostic rather than approximate the source.
A release MUST refuse an unpaired surrogate, a number that is not finite, an integer outside the safe range, and negative zero, rather than serialize a value two readers would read differently.
An incompatible change to such a format increments its own major version, and a package version MUST NOT stand in for that declaration.
A reader accepts a value it does not know, so adding a value to one is compatible, and a release MUST NOT withdraw a value or give it another meaning within a major version of the format.
The shape of each major version of such a format, and whether its readers refuse unknown fields, MUST be recorded in the repository and compared with the declarations the built packages publish.
A release MUST NOT change correctness-bearing locale matching, message evaluation, function behavior, XLIFF mapping, identity, or canonicalization through an ordinary dependency update.
The dependency sets of the published packages MUST be exactly those stated here.
Node-only code, Node-only dependencies, Node globals, and compiler APIs MUST NOT enter `@neolorn/equator` or a consumer's browser bundle.
Angular server rendering is a runtime concern, and a release MUST NOT require the toolkit to be installed for it.
A release MUST NOT subdivide the primary entry point on any other ground.

It MUST NOT ship the pseudo-localization transform, which is build-time work under `10-compiler-and-tooling.spec.md`: shipping it in a runtime entry point would put it in a production bundle behind a flag.
A consumer MUST import only declared package exports.
Such an export is not part of the supported contract, the reference omits it, and a consumer MUST NOT import it.
An Angular-free entry point MUST NOT import `@angular/*` in its JavaScript or in its type declarations.
An entry point MUST NOT reach into another entry point's sources by a relative path.
A base entry point MUST NOT depend on an entry point above it.
Importing the toolkit API MUST NOT execute a command, mutate the process, install a hook, scan a project, write a file, start a watcher, or perform network access.
`@neolorn/equator` MUST be distributed in Angular Package Format with partial Angular compilation.

Its distributable MUST carry: - ESM output in the format the supported Angular line requires; - an explicit export map naming every entry point; - generated TypeScript declarations, with declaration maps; - source maps whose paths are portable and reveal nothing about the machine that built them; - accurate side-effect metadata; - whatever the consuming Angular compiler needs to complete compilation.

A release uses Angular's supported library packaging pipeline; a replacement for it MUST prove the same format, export integrity, partial compilation, declaration quality, and consumer compatibility before it is used.
entries.reason: This governs the order in which a different build pipeline may be adopted, which is a decision made before any release exists to test. Whatever pipeline builds a release, its output meets the same format, export and declaration checks in verify:packages and the consumer rows, and those are mapped under the statements that name each property.

entries.statement: Both distributables MUST remain installable by any npm-compatible package manager.
An optional integration MUST NOT put its peer, or its implementation dependency, on the primary entry point.
A release MUST NOT bundle or privately own a second Angular or RxJS instance.
It MUST NOT have to assemble the toolkit's compiler machinery from parts.
Installing a package of a release MUST NOT run a migration, a generation step, or any other work of its own.

A runtime module MUST be free of side effects on import, and importing `@neolorn/equator` MUST NOT: - load locale data or a catalog; - start a timer, watcher, worker, or network request; - read or mutate the document, the Router, storage, or global state; - register a platform effect or application state; - install a service worker or a persistence mechanism.
Package metadata MUST let a consumer's build remove what it does not use.
Testing code, optional integrations, toolkit code, Node-only dependencies, unused locales, and unselected providers MUST stay unreachable from a production graph that does not select them.
A release declares the ranges it is installable within and the rows it has been verified on, and MUST NOT present the first as the second.

Every other statement of a supported range, in a gate, a verification row, a generated page or a sentence, MUST be read from those manifests, and changing what a release supports MUST be done by changing a manifest.
It MUST be pinned against the manifests by package verification, so a manifest that moves without it fails rather than ships.
A combination inside a declared range that nothing has executed is installable and not verified, and a release MUST NOT describe it as supported.
A release MUST NOT claim a host outside these ranges, and MUST NOT imply that verifying one combination verifies every combination a range admits.
The toolkit MUST detect an unsupported Angular or TypeScript host before it does compiler work and fail with an actionable diagnostic, rather than attempt a best-effort private compatibility.
Toolkit integration with Angular and TypeScript MUST use documented, supported APIs behind toolkit-owned adapters.
A private API MUST NOT become a dependency a consumer can reach.

Verification MUST establish, for each package: - the distribution format and, for the runtime, partial compilation; - the export map, the declarations, the declaration maps, and the side-effect metadata; - that one Angular and one RxJS instance are present in a consumer's graph; - that TypeScript and the package manager resolve every declared subpath; - that the browser and the server rendering paths both work; - that the toolkit is absent from a browser bundle; - that testing code and unselected optional capabilities are absent from a consumer that does not select them; - that no consumer path, machine-absolute path, temporary location, or generated consumer path appears in published metadata, maps, or declarations.
A consumer's do not, and a map, a declaration, or any other published file MUST NOT carry an absolute local path.
A release MUST derive every locale-dependent table from the one declaration.
Canonicalization MUST be deterministic across the toolkit, the server, and the browser.
A difference between runtimes MUST NOT change an identity anything compares, stores, or exchanges.
Likely-subtag maximization MAY inform matching and direction analysis.
entries.reason: This grants a permission to use maximization in two places; a release that did not use it would still conform, so there is no behavior to withdraw. The limit on that permission is the next statement, which has its own check.

entries.statement: A release MUST refuse that way a value that is not text, a tag the platform does not parse, with the platform's error as the cause, and a tag that names no script and has none in the likely subtags data, so one function refuses in one class.
It MUST NOT rewrite a declared identity, a catalog key, a URL value, a cache key, or a persisted preference.
A release MUST reject one where a catalog takes its identity, and therefore where a catalog key, a cache key, a URL value, or a persisted preference does.

Untrusted locale text is bounded in length and complexity, and a release MUST NOT use it directly as an identity, a path, a cache key, a protocol field, a stored value, or the payload of a diagnostic.

A release MUST give root as the main parent of a locale that is a language and a script other than the likely script of that language, the `nonlikelyScript` rule of the same section, whether or not the pinned list names the locale: the list is a subset kept for migration, and `ru-Latn` inherits from nothing although no entry names it.

A release MUST give a language_region whose likely script differs from its language's, where the pinned list declares no parent for it, the parent language_script_region in every component: `zh-TW` inherits through `zh-Hant-TW` and `zh-Hant` and never through `zh`, which is written in the other script, and `sr-ME` through `sr-Latn-ME` and `sr-Latn`.
A declared parent may change the language, and a release MUST follow that rather than narrow the pinned data.

The rule keeps text in one script from inheriting text in another, so a release MUST NOT apply it along the chain of a pseudo-locale: `en-Arab-XB`, which UTS #35 Part 1 describes by its region as a "derived testing locale with forced RTL English", inherits through `en-Arab` to `en`.

An alias that collides with a supported locale, shadows one, forms a cycle, or names a locale the consumer does not support is an error, and a release MUST refuse the configuration rather than pick a reading of it.
A release MUST NOT read the script or region dimensions of that data as distances.
Every source except `default` MAY decline, and answering the default in place of a source that declined would make every later source unreachable.
It is a decision already taken rather than a preference to be weighed, and an invalid one MUST return a typed failure and change no state.
A request for Traditional Chinese MUST NOT be answered in Simplified, so the script is compared.

Resolution is sensitive to which source answered: - an address and an explicit selection use exact canonical identity or a declared alias; - a recognized noncanonical address is handled by the routing canonicalization contract in `07-routing-rendering-and-seo.spec.md`; - malformed or unsupported locale intent in an address MUST NOT render another language at that address; - a stored value that no longer canonicalizes to a supported locale is excluded, with a bounded diagnostic that MUST NOT echo the value; - a language preference list honors its order and its quality values; - automatic matching MUST NOT cross base languages or choose an incompatible script; - a contradiction in trusted configuration MUST fail before use rather than degrade into a preference.
A release MUST NOT reorder or merge them.

A locale that initialization resolved MUST NOT be written back: persisting it would turn the first negotiated answer into a permanent one, and a later change to the visitor's own preferences would stop having any effect.
A release MUST supply the two separately: one operation that forgets what is stored and leaves the page where it is, and one locale change that moves the page without recording a choice.
A release MUST report a removal that could not reach every store, because a removal reported as complete while a store still holds the value leaves the choice in force.

A release MUST keep the persistence port implementable without it and MUST treat a store that offers none as a store the removal did not reach, because the port is what a consumer application writes against and a release that added a required method to it would stop every store written against the previous one from compiling.
A persistence failure MUST NOT corrupt active state, and a write for an older decision MUST NOT supersede a newer one.

A page the server drew or a build wrote is adopted as it was decided, as `06-runtime-and-angular.spec.md` section 10 requires, and once hydration is complete a release MUST read the stores again, so that a stored choice the declared sources would choose for the address moves the page.

A value read this way, or when a page returns from the browser's back-forward cache, MUST NOT move the page if the visitor asked for a locale change or a removal while it was being read: that request is the newer decision.

A release MUST report to the observability sink each way such a read ends, whether it moves the page or leaves it where it is, and each reason the stores were not read, each as an event none of the others produces, because a page left in the wrong language by a read that found nothing looks, from outside, the same as one whose stores were never read.
The locale cookie a release writes, from its browser store or from its own request handler, MUST be one a browser stores.

A release MUST refuse at configuration a cookie name that is not a token, a path or domain a `Set-Cookie` header cannot carry, a lifetime that is not a positive number of seconds, and an attribute combination the browser's cookie storage model discards, such as `SameSite=None` without `Secure` or a `__Host-` name with a domain.
A release MUST make each of those refusals an `invalid-configuration` failure, as it makes every other option it refuses.
A consumer MAY set a strict policy instead, which refuses the source-locale result and accepts an inherited one.
Fallback MUST NOT accept invalid syntax, incompatible inputs, unsafe rich structure, or an incompatible artifact, and MUST NOT emit a raw key, a parser detail, or an unexplained empty value.

entries.section: 10. Content that is not a fallback
entries.statement: Consumer-owned content is not a message, and a release MUST NOT apply message fallback to it.

entries.section: 10. Content that is not a fallback
entries.statement: The unknown state is stated rather than left absent, and a release MUST classify these cases so a consumer can tell them apart.

entries.section: 10. Content that is not a fallback
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT inspect that content or record a conclusion about it, because assigning a direction to content whose direction is unknown states as fact something a release has no basis for.

entries.section: 10. Content that is not a fallback
entries.statement: It MUST NOT detect, translate, rewrite, moderate, store, or decide the authoritative language of a consumer's content.
A release MUST supply an accessible renderer for that payload, announced to assistive technology, carrying the language and direction of the message it renders, and offering a retry.
Inline prose, template text, an extracted default, and a code literal MUST NOT become a second authoring authority.
Tooling MAY propose a catalog edit a person reviews.
entries.reason: This permits a kind of tool to exist and requires nothing of a release, so no behavior of a release can break it.

entries.statement: A release MUST refuse a catalog that constructs anything executable, and MUST NOT resolve a schema, a tag, or an entity over the network while reading one.
A release MUST NOT require those concerns to coincide, and MUST NOT refuse a scope for its breadth, or for its name unless the name is reserved.
A release MUST refuse a scope with a reserved name at generation, with a diagnostic that names the path it could not write, and MUST NOT write one generated module over another.

A consumer's domain records are runtime data from a release's point of view, wherever they are stored, and a release MUST NOT turn one into a message identity, compiled data, a generated contract, a cache entry, or part of a localization snapshot.
An empty provider, scope, or typed registry MUST NOT be generated as scaffolding for something that does not exist yet.
Locale is a representation dimension and MUST NOT be part of identity.
It MUST NOT be read as a URL, a discovery location, a registry lookup, an environment, a version, or proof of ownership.
entries.reason: The provider identifier is only ever compared as an exact string, and no code path resolves, fetches or looks it up, so there is no behavior a small edit could withdraw; the statement forbids an interpretation the release does not contain.

entries.statement: A release MUST refuse identity, locale, ownership, revision, approval, ticket, vendor, or other workflow fields inside an entry.
`description` and `context` are the durable translator-guidance fields this model provides in place of comments, and they MUST NOT be used interchangeably.
A target entry MAY carry its own `description` or `context` where guidance is locale-specific, and otherwise the source entry's guidance applies.
A target entry uses the same three forms and MUST NOT declare `inputs` or `slots`: it inherits the effective source contract.

The toolkit derives the variables, selectors, functions, operand types, and uses from it before any refinement: - an unannotated external variable is a required, non-nullable string; - a variable annotated by a function takes that function's operand type; - incompatible uses of one variable fail validation rather than widening or coercing it; - a target may omit an input its own grammar does not need, and MUST NOT add one or change its type, its optionality, or its nullability.
Where the standard leaves a behavior implementation-defined, a release MUST resolve it as a refusal at compile time, and MUST NOT resolve it as a fallback value or a thrown error at render time.

A release MUST judge a `calendar` option by how a calendar's name is written and a `timeZone` option by the names the pinned time-zone database carries, as `08-formatting-parsing-and-domain.spec.md` section 2 states both, and MUST NOT ask the host about either.

A release MUST judge a `unit` option, and the options a numeric expression resolves to taken together, by the rules the pinned ECMA-402 edition gives the `Intl.NumberFormat` constructor, reading the units that edition sanctions from its own text and the fraction digits a currency is written with from the pinned CLDR release, and MUST NOT ask the host.

A release MUST refuse such an option set where the message is compiled, declaring the combination unsupported as `01-standards-profile.spec.md` section 5 permits, rather than compile a message that would throw where it is rendered.
Inheritance MUST NOT become a second way past a closed descriptor.

A release MUST call the function, or build the slot, without an option whose variable was omitted or is null, MUST leave in force what the operand carried under that name, and MUST refuse the call where the function requires the option.
Each key is the exact inferred external variable name without `$`, and a release MUST refuse a key that introduces a new, misspelled, or unused input.

A refinement is either a portable type identifier, meaning `{ type: <type-id> }`, or a record containing only `type`, `enum`, `optional`, `nullable`, and `description`: - `type` resolves through a release's portable operand-type registry, and MUST NOT be a TypeScript symbol, an import, a type expression, or a source path; - `enum` is a nonempty sequence of unique literal values compatible with the effective type, and `null` is governed only by `nullable`; - `optional` and `nullable` are independent booleans defaulting to false: `optional` permits omission or `undefined`, `nullable` permits an explicit `null`; - neither creates a default value.
It MUST NOT contradict MessageFormat syntax or a registered function contract, and MUST NOT declare a default, a substitution, a coercion, or a conversion.
A release MUST NOT coerce the value, substitute a permitted member, or interpolate the invalid value.

A MessageFormat markup name is a semantic slot identifier, and a release MUST NOT read it as an HTML element, a component, a template, an import, a style, a destination, a callback, or executable configuration.
A target catalog MUST NOT contain `slots` and inherits the effective source contract.

An expanded refinement contains only: - `kind`, resolved through the portable slot-kind registry. Omitting it selects a required message-local trusted binding, and it MUST NOT infer a component, template, element, URL, action, callback, class, style, or implementation symbol. - `shape`, exactly `paired` or `standalone`, required only where a source-unused slot is allowed and its kind does not determine the shape. - `optional` and `repeatable`, independent booleans. False and false is exactly one; true and false is zero or one; false and true is one or more; true and true is zero or more within the global resource bounds. - `within`, a nonempty sequence of allowed immediate parent slot names or the reserved `@root`. It may narrow a compatible placement and MUST NOT weaken a registered or global nesting constraint. - `description`, translator guidance for the case where the slot's use, its name, and its registered kind are not enough.
It MUST NOT invent a slot, alter a kind or a shape, exceed cardinality, remove a required semantic action, or edit protected implementation data.
A catalog MAY control an option only where a registered kind declares a closed, typed, bounded, translation-safe semantic option.
entries.reason: This grants a catalog a permission; its restrictive half is the prohibition in the next statement, which is where a check belongs.

entries.statement: A catalog MUST NOT control HTML, a URL, a route, a component, a template, a class, a style, a color, a DOM property, an accessibility role, a permission, a sanitizer, a callback, or any executable behavior.
An interactive slot MUST NOT contain or be contained by another interactive slot.
Every rich contract has a deterministic safe text projection, and a standalone custom kind MUST provide one.
Application code passes handles to the runtime's APIs and MUST NOT construct a qualified string to stand in for one.
The toolkit keeps each selected handle's relationship to its own contracts and MUST NOT widen a heterogeneous choice into an untyped parameter map.
It is scope-local, MUST NOT appear in a target catalog, and is omitted where a scope has none.
A template MUST NOT use a glob, a regular expression, an optional or repeated part, alternation, recursion, an executable predicate, or runtime concatenation.
A `segments` key MUST match a placeholder exactly, and its value is a portable registered identifier-segment type with deterministic validation and a canonical one-part serialization.
At least one current source message MUST match the template.
The toolkit derives the common effective input and rich-slot contract from the current matches, and every current and future member MUST satisfy it.
A release MUST NOT require a per-message family field, an enrollment list, an include or exclude list, an alias table, or a duplicate ledger.
Matching a template MUST NOT by itself invent or authorize a message.
A release MUST NOT expose an unrestricted lookup by arbitrary string, and MUST NOT perform a fuzzy match, a hidden alias lookup, or a guessed prefix.
A release MUST NOT fail a build on that advisory by default; a stricter freshness or completeness policy is opt-in.
It carries nothing else, and a release MUST refuse one whose top level is not exactly that set of fields.

MessageFormat's syntax gives every expression a literal, a variable, or a function, so a release MUST refuse an expression that names neither an operand nor a function with a typed failure, and MUST NOT print it as empty text.

A release MUST refuse a candidate carrying a function, a getter, a setter, a prototype other than the plain object prototype, a cycle, an import reference, a template, or a dynamically compiled expression, rather than evaluate around it.
Catalog data names a descriptor identity, and an artifact MUST NOT supply the implementation behind one.
A release MAY deliver a catalog compiled and deployed as part of one application build through a lazy ES module, as a code-splitting wrapper.
entries.reason: This permits one delivery mechanism and obliges a release to nothing, so no behavior can violate it.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT let a transport wrapper grant a catalog authority the catalog does not have.

It carries its own profile label, the committed locale, the formatting context, an optional route record, the catalogs, and the participant records, and a release MUST NOT put a function, a template, or a consumer's domain payload into it.
A release MUST bound and revalidate every field of it before adopting any of it, and MUST discard the whole transfer when any part is unrecognized rather than repair the part it can read.
Every digest a release writes is `sha256-` followed by 43 unpadded base64url characters, and a release MUST refuse a value that does not match that shape wherever one is read.
It does not prove semantic validity, compatibility, safety, or permission to run, and a release MUST NOT treat it as proving any of them.
A release MUST return a failure for an error at any of those steps and MUST NOT write any part of the output.

A release MUST establish, before it accepts a generated set, that: - the descriptor's profile, generated ABI, application-contract fingerprint, and semantic-registry fingerprint match the generated configuration; - every artifact names a configured scope and a configured locale; - every artifact's compiled profile, schema, standards profile, and generated ABI are ones this release supports, and its required features are all supported, where a feature that depends on the application, such as a formatting context that names a time zone, is supported only when the application supplies it; - every artifact's fingerprints and required extension descriptors match its scope's; - every artifact's content digest is well formed and its resource summary is within the fixed ceilings; - no two artifacts claim the same catalog identity, and a loader exists for each one; - the set is not empty.

A release MUST establish, before it accepts one loaded candidate, that the candidate is inert JSON within the snapshot ceilings, that its fields are exactly the ones section 1 names, that its key, profiles, fingerprints, and required extensions equal the address it was loaded for, that its resource summary equals both the recorded summary and a summary re-measured from its own content, and that its content digest recomputed over its canonical form equals the recorded digest.
A release MUST reject the catalog an admission failure names and MUST NOT replace the committed localization state with it.
A rejected candidate is never remembered, and a release MUST NOT let an address verified once stand in for a later candidate offered under that address.
A release MUST NOT treat it as a network publisher, an origin, a signing key, an authorization realm, or an acquisition endpoint.
entries.reason: The provider identity is used only as part of an exact-match key and a fingerprint input, and no code fetches from, verifies against or authorizes by it, so there is no behavior a small edit could withdraw; the statement forbids an interpretation the release does not contain.

entries.statement: Their authority, their artifact identities, and their catalog-set identities stay distinct, and a release MUST NOT collapse them into one provider or one set.
A release MUST refuse to use an artifact until every descriptor that artifact requires is bound to a registered implementation whose descriptor canonicalizes identically.
An artifact's compatibility identity is its own scope's, and a release MUST NOT let a change confined to another scope change that artifact's address.

A release MUST refuse a catalog whose compiled content exceeds a compile-time ceiling, and MUST refuse a candidate whose recorded summary and re-measured summary disagree or whose measurements exceed a runtime ceiling.
An artifact MUST NOT raise one, and a consumer MUST NOT be given a way to raise one.
entries.reason: The ceilings are frozen constants compared against measured values, and neither the artifact format nor the public setup has a field that feeds them, so there is no path a small edit could open without adding a new option; the statement forbids a capability the release does not contain.

entries.statement: A release MUST require no network, no backend, no content or translation management system, no service worker, no persistent cache, no credential, no signing key, and no hosted service for it.
A release MUST NOT report it as a load failure, so that a caller can tell an untranslated scope from a broken one.
The loader map is copied into a null-prototype frozen map before use, and a release MUST refuse an entry that is an accessor or is not a function.
It shares the in-flight request for the same catalog identity and it is cancellable, and a release MUST NOT let it commit a locale or any other state.
A release MUST still observe its failure, and MUST NOT leave it as a rejection nobody handles.
A release defines no network retry, persistent store, offline mode, service-worker cache, or remote source discovery, and a release MUST NOT introduce one behind this contract.
A release MUST join a second request for a catalog already loading to the first rather than start a second load.
Eviction is automatic and takes the least recently used unpinned entry, and a release MUST NOT evict a pinned one.
A release MUST NOT turn a failed load into a cache entry, and MUST release everything a disposed context cached.
A release MUST NOT make a credential, a user identifier, a consumer's domain value, translated content, or a participant payload a cache key or a cache entry.
entries.reason: The store's keys are built only from the provider, scope and locale, and the admission key only from address fields read from the generated descriptor; no argument carries anything else into either, so there is no behavior a small edit could withdraw without adding a new input.

entries.statement: Pages, products, articles, comments, user-authored values, and other consumer records stay in the consumer's own services, stores, signals, and components, and a release MUST NOT admit one into compiled data, a descriptor, loader state, cache state, or a localization snapshot.
A release MUST NOT echo the value that failed, because a diagnostic is written to a log that is read somewhere else.
A release MUST accept feature providers as the only other argument to either.

A release MUST apply the document language and direction, restore focus, selection, and scroll position across a locale change, and announce the change to assistive technology, all without a provider, and MUST offer a withdrawal of the document effects for an application rendering inside a host page that owns the document itself.
A release MUST evaluate a handle synchronously once the scope holding it is ready, and MUST NOT start a catalog load, a network request, or any other deferred work from an evaluation call.
A release MUST NOT convert a structured result into trusted markup on its own; `09-safe-content-and-ux.spec.md` owns what may be trusted.
A release MUST report the supplying locale on the result rather than assume it is the committed primary locale.
A release MUST raise a typed error naming the scope, and MUST NOT load the scope implicitly or return the identifier as text.

A release MUST work in a zoneless, OnPush application through Angular's documented signal and scheduling contracts, and MUST NOT depend on `zone.js`, a manual change-detection sweep, or an undocumented lifecycle order.
Every pipe reads the ambient snapshot, so a release MUST declare each one impure.

A formatting pipe is typed to one canonical value kind and to the options that kind leaves open, MUST render an empty string when its formatter reports, and MUST report that diagnostic through the observability sink.

entries.section: 4. The snapshot and the three locale roles
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT admit a consumer record, a participant payload, an acquisition result, or a credential into a snapshot.

entries.section: 4. The snapshot and the three locale roles
entries.statement: Three locales are distinct and a release MUST keep them so.

entries.section: 4. The snapshot and the three locale roles
entries.statement: A scope may be loaded without being required by the current view, and a release MUST NOT commit a snapshot whose required scopes are not all ready in the primary locale.

entries.section: 4. The snapshot and the three locale roles
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT let a consumer application mutate that state or construct a snapshot it will accept.
A release MUST coalesce equivalent concurrent initialization, and MUST NOT publish a partial runtime.
When no initial snapshot can be built, a release MUST expose a typed failure and the generated recovery payload.

A recovery message that cannot be evaluated MUST NOT replace that failure: the initialization still ends with the reason no snapshot could be built, the message is left out, and its own failure is reported to the observability sink.
A failed initialization MUST NOT move the address the reader asked for.
In a browser a release MUST hold the navigation to that address until a retry succeeds and then complete it, so a retry brings the reader to the page they asked for, in the locale its address states.
A server render has no retry to wait for, and a release MUST NOT hold one.
A server render or prerender whose initial snapshot cannot be built MUST fail rather than render the recovery payload, so the deployment answers with its own error and a build stops.

A child context may be created for a route or a component subtree; it inherits what it does not state, owns its own lifetime, and a release MUST NOT let it mutate or leak into its parent, a sibling, or another request.

A release MUST create an adapter that holds request state in the context that owns it rather than in the application configuration, because one configuration object serves every concurrent server-rendered request and the first context destroyed would dispose the adapter for all of them.
A release MUST share nothing else between contexts except validated immutable catalog artifacts whose identity proves them interchangeable.
A release MUST refuse a request that names any other mode with the `invalid-configuration` diagnostic, and MUST NOT start a transition for it.

The Router integration is configured with the mode its navigations change locale in, and a release MUST refuse a mode that is neither with the same diagnostic where that configuration is given, and MUST NOT leave it to the first navigation.

In coordinated mode a release MUST validate the request, resolve the route and formatting context, load and admit every required scope, wait for every required participant, build one candidate snapshot, and keep the current view rendered and usable until that candidate commits.
A scope a coordinated change names as progressive is required by that change, and a release MUST load and admit it before the candidate commits.
A release MUST refuse a change that names one scope as both required and progressive with the `invalid-configuration` diagnostic, and MUST NOT start a transition for it.
A scope the committed snapshot requires is not thereby named as required, and a release MUST NOT refuse a change that names such a scope as progressive.
A progressive change that names no required scope MUST leave that scope out of the scopes it waits for and load it alongside, unless a scope request is still waiting for it.

In progressive mode a release MAY commit the primary locale and the ready scopes while registered regions finish independently, and MUST expose each region's transition identity, readiness, outcome, supplying locale, and direction.
A release MUST NOT decide whether such a region shows a placeholder, keeps its old content, hides itself, retries, or substitutes something else.

A release MUST NOT let a locale change requested while the context is initializing end that initialization, or be ended by it: the change waits for the initialization to settle, the initialization commits what it was preparing, and the change then runs from that snapshot.

A release MUST coalesce equivalent in-flight requests, MUST let the latest distinct intent win, and MUST NOT let a superseded transition commit, persist, or overwrite the diagnostics of the current one.

In coordinated mode a release MUST leave the prior address, view, snapshot, document state, focus, and persistence unchanged when a transition is cancelled, a guard rejects it, or its preparation fails.
In progressive mode a release MUST confine a region's failure to that region and MUST NOT roll back an already valid commit.
A release MUST hand a participant the target locale, the effective formatting context, the transition identity, and a cancellation signal, and nothing else about the transition.
A release MUST NOT read, copy, cache, or transfer that payload.
A release MUST preserve the last two without reinterpreting either, and MUST NOT turn a missing translation into a domain outcome or a domain outcome into a localization failure.

A consumer application that serves content from a locale other than the target one MUST report ready with that locale as the supplying locale rather than report unavailable, so the region can declare the language it is really in.
entries.reason: This binds the application's participant, which decides what it reports; the release cannot know which locale the application's content came from. What the release owes, keeping the reported supplying locale, is checked by the locale-bound representation validation.

entries.statement: A consumer application MAY set a cancellable deadline on a participant; expiry is an operational failure and MUST NOT authorize an incomplete coordinated commit.

A release MUST abort that signal when the change is abandoned or overtaken at any moment before the participant commits or is discarded, including after it has reported, and MUST NOT ask a participant whose signal is aborted to commit.
A release MUST refuse a commit that answers with a promise as a participant contract rejection, and that refusal fails the transition.

A rollback, a discard, and a disposal are told of an outcome that is already decided, so a release MUST report one that answers with a promise as the same rejection, naming the participant, and MUST NOT let it replace that outcome.
A context built outside the injector MAY be given a request context, a value of the consumer application's own.
entries.reason: This permits a caller to give a context a value of its own and obliges nothing by itself. What a release does with a value that was given is the next statement.

entries.statement: A release MUST hand that value, unread and unchanged, to every participant of that context and of a child context made from it, and MUST NOT hand a participant a request context the consumer application did not give.
A release MUST NOT require a consumer application to list startup scopes or per-route scopes.
Startup means loaded for the locale the page started in, so a release MUST have every scope the current view renders ready in the target locale before a coordinated commit, startup scopes included.

A release MUST hold a newly activated scope behind its readiness boundary or keep its previous compatible content, MUST NOT publish a partial scope, and MUST NOT present a catalog from an unrelated locale as the committed target.

A coordinated change commits only once everything the view renders is ready, so in coordinated mode a release MUST load a scope a route names as progressive before the navigation completes, as it loads a required one.
In such a render a release MUST load a scope a route names as progressive before the render completes, as it loads a required one.
A release MUST NOT emit a meaningful localized representation before the primary locale and the startup scopes of that request are ready.

A release MUST adopt the transferred primary locale, catalog set, route projection, direction, and formatting context before any later transition, MUST NOT renegotiate the locale during hydration, and MUST NOT reload a catalog the transfer already carried.

Angular's ordinary update pass then finds the stored binding value no longer matching the committed locale and writes the current value over the claimed DOM, so a release MUST NOT ship a repair for a deferred block.
entries.reason: This forbids adding a mechanism whose job Angular already does, so a release with or without it renders the same page; there is no runtime behavior that tells the two apart. The observable requirement, that content in a deferred block ends up in the committed locale, is the next statement.

entries.statement: What has to hold is stated here as a rule so that a framework change leaving a claimed boundary stale would be caught: a release MUST keep localized content inside a hydration boundary part of the committed representation, and a consumer application MUST NOT place localized content behind a boundary that public Angular APIs cannot hydrate or replace coherently.

A release MUST run persistence, the announcement, and comparable non-visual effects after the commit they belong to, MUST carry the transition identity into each, and MUST NOT let an older completion overwrite a newer selection.
A release MUST report a persistence failure and MUST NOT roll back an otherwise valid commit for one.
When a coherence-critical effect fails, a release MUST either prevent the commit or trigger complete recovery, and MUST NOT leave false document state behind either.
A release MUST NOT let that disposal reach another context or a consumer application's own store.
Where the injector that owns the context is destroyed during that wait, a release MUST NOT reject that promise with the disposal, because no start is left for it to stop and nothing would handle it.

A release MUST report every scope of a destroyed context as failed with the typed disposed failure, one that was ready when the context was destroyed included, and MUST NOT go on reporting the readiness the scope had.

A release MUST NOT start further work in a context that was destroyed by a hook or a participant it told of a commit: no progressive scope load, no participant preparation, and no return to the ready state.
A release MUST provide deterministic control over deferred loading and participant outcomes through them, without a network call and without shared global state.

A release MUST supply the seat, MUST answer through the same request handler a deployment uses rather than through a second implementation of the same rules, and MUST NOT require a listening socket, a built bundle, or a browser to use it.

An address of any other scheme names no origin a deployment answers at, and a release MUST hand it to the handler as written, where it is refused as a structurally unsafe target, rather than answer it on another origin.
A release MUST leave a numeric reference that names no character, which is code point zero, a surrogate, or a value past the last code point, as it was written.
A release MUST make a declared page outcome observable through that seat.
A release MUST export that reset and MUST use it in its own documented testing recipe.

A render table reads it to apply section 9 of `07-routing-rendering-and-seo.spec.md`, and a release MUST mark with it the formatting context it builds for that locale, so the locale formats in its language with what its formatting declares, as section 4 of `08-formatting-parsing-and-domain.spec.md` states.
A release MUST NOT carry the mark in the state a server render transfers: the browser's own generated configuration says it again.
A release MUST derive one deterministic localized route and metadata projection from them, and MUST NOT require a consumer application to maintain a second route manifest beside them.

A release MUST report which declarations hide addresses from the projection and MUST NOT fail the build for it, because hiding routes from static analysis is a legitimate shape for an application to have.
A release MUST derive that identity from the route's full path, keeping literal segments as their text and collapsing every parameter segment to one mark, so renaming a parameter changes no identity.
A release MUST NOT machine-translate route text.
entries.reason: The release has no step that writes route text: every localized spelling comes from paths and parameter spellings the application declares, so there is no translating behavior for an injection to add or withdraw.

entries.statement: A release MUST report both and project neither, and MUST report an address it cannot name within the identity grammar the same way.

For every locale the policy names, a release MUST check that serializing a value and parsing the result back succeeds and serializes to the same text, MUST run that check on every build, and MUST refuse where the address is built, naming the route, the parameter, and the locale.
An inbound address whose parameter the codec declines to parse means the route does not match, and a release MUST hand that address back unchanged for the application to answer.
A release MUST fail the call with a typed failure that names the route, the parameter, and the locale where one is asked for, and keeps the thrown error as its cause.
The request handler MUST answer that failure as it answers a render that failed, and MUST NOT answer the address as not found.

The codecs a release ships are codecs under the same contract: each MUST decline a value it refuses by writing nothing, so an address built from that value is refused as a route with no address there, and a release MUST NOT report that refusal as a codec that threw.
A release MUST fall back to the codec for a locale the declaration omits, and MUST drop a locale with no spelling from the alternate cluster rather than guess one.

A release MUST stamp it with the navigation that made it, MUST replace the standing declaration outright when a navigation commits, including when the arriving page declares nothing, and MUST answer a reader that names a navigation rather than a reader that asks for whichever declaration is current.
A release MUST project the document again when a declaration arrives, not only when a navigation commits.

A release MUST require it to be a safe path segment that parses under the route's own codec, and MUST NOT impose the codec's round-trip check on it, because in another locale the parameter's value is that locale's spelling and requiring the two to match would reject every correct declaration.

A release MUST fail compilation for a URL built against an identity that does not exist or a parameter contract that is unsatisfied, rather than throw from a function whose declared result is a string, and MUST require a projection containing a parameterized route to supply that route's codecs.
A release MUST NOT guess a spelling for a route whose codec has been removed since: the route matches no address, and building or prerendering its address is refused as a configuration error.

A consumer application declares the policy exactly once, and a release MUST NOT accept it from a second provider, because the URL locale source, the canonical URLs, the reciprocal alternates, the redirects, and the Router adapter all read that one declaration.

A release MUST refuse a policy kind it does not serve at configuration time, naming the kinds it does serve, and MUST NOT warn and continue, because a diagnostic that starts anyway is silent in production and leaves the application in a state no rule describes.

A release MUST hold a policy to the tables a constructor writes wherever it reads one, and MUST refuse one that departs from them as a configuration error: a locale that is not a canonical tag, a default locale the policy does not name, a prefix, alias, or locale-neutral root that is not a path segment or repeats another, an origin that is not a normalized HTTP origin, a prefix or origin table that does not read each address back to the locale it was written for, or a member that belongs to another kind of policy.

A release MUST refuse a value of another kind, `null` included, with the `invalid-configuration` diagnostic where the configuration is given, and MUST NOT read text as a table of its characters, a number as an empty table, or an object as a list.

A release MUST intersect the declared policy with the generated configuration once, into a narrowed policy, and MUST resolve, publish, and provide from that value alone, so a site added later inherits the intersection rather than repeating it.

A locale the policy names and the build did not generate gets no prerendered file, no server route, no alternate claim, and no client route branch, and a release MUST treat its prefix as unsupported locale intent and ignore a remembered preference naming it.
A release MUST refuse outright a configuration that omits the policy's own default locale, because filtering that one leaves an application with no addresses at all.
A release MUST NOT compare a locale table it read in part, because the locales it could not read would be reported as configured and unaddressed in an application that addresses them.

A release MUST name, in an advisory that blocks no build, each option of the policy it did not read, and MUST say there that neither comparison was made for what those options hold, because a build that stays silent about a policy it could not read is read as a build that found the policy right.

A release MUST be told which origin this build answers at, MUST require it to be one of the policy's own including its scheme, and MUST refuse a missing or unnamed origin at configuration, because otherwise every request answers 400, a prerender writes no files, and the build still succeeds.

A release MUST refuse a context whose origin is anything else, under every policy kind, and MUST NOT read the address at the default locale's origin instead, because that answers in a locale the request did not ask for.
A release MUST advertise or link a locale only where arriving at the address with nothing said about preference yields that locale.

A consumer application's host MUST reject a structurally unsafe target, meaning invalid encoding, an encoded separator, a control character, a duplicate separator, a backslash, a dot segment, or another ambiguous form, at its earliest boundary, before Angular routing, server rendering, locale resolution, catalog loading, or a domain lookup.
entries.reason: This binds the host an application deploys in front of its own code, which the release does not ship. Where the release is that boundary, in its request handler and adapter, statement 22 carries the check.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT repair or reflect one.
Where a release is itself that boundary, in its own request handler and the adapter that feeds it, the rejection is the release's own and it MUST classify the target as it arrived.

Presentation routing has two entrances and a release MUST delocalize at both, through one function: the localized location strategy for an address the browser supplies, and the localized URL handling strategy for an address the application hands the router.
A release MUST preserve a consumer-domain outcome without reinterpreting it, and MUST NOT turn a missing translation into a missing entity.
A release MUST NOT let an address the locale policy declines reach that composition, because it is not an outcome; it goes to the deployment's own handling.

A refused target MUST NOT reach it either: a structurally unsafe target has no presentation, it carries a diagnostic rather than a route, and asking an application to draw a page for one asks it to draw an address the release has just refused.
Two answers a renderer can give are not routing outcomes, and a release MUST keep the renderer's status for both.
A release MUST send either with no content and MUST compose its own fields onto it as it does onto a page.

On a 304 those are the fields RFC 9110 section 15.4.5 requires a 304 to repeat from the 200 it stands for, the cache directives and the varying fields, and a release MUST NOT add other representation metadata to it.

A release MUST NOT answer 200 for a render that carried no content, because a cache that stores that answer holds an empty page for the address, and one classified as shared gives that page to every later reader.

A release MUST send that status, MUST classify the response as private and not stored, and MUST mark it not to be indexed, whatever the address's own classification and indexing class are, because sent as the address's 200 an error page is one a shared cache keeps for the address and a crawler indexes as its content.
That status is still not a declaration, and a release MUST NOT treat it as one.

A server evaluates a precondition only where its answer without it would have been successful (RFC 9110 section 13.2.1), so a release MUST NOT hand a renderer the request's preconditions where the address resolved to any other outcome.

A redirect the runtime issues during a render, such as the correction to a parameter spelling a page declared, is a routing outcome, and a release MUST give it the status the table below gives it, through the response channel the render shares with the handler.

A release MUST answer preference-dependent locale entry with 307 for safe methods, deterministic canonical correction or declared replacement with 308, unsupported explicit locale intent with 404 at the requested URL, a missing route or an absent entity with the localized 404 at the requested URL, a declared permanent removal with no replacement with 410, and a structurally unsafe target with 400 before presentation routing.
A release MUST NOT render another language as the locale that was asked for.
A release MUST supply a declaration that carries both, and a release that supplies none leaves a consumer application with no way to state either at an address that resolved.
A release MUST accept the declaration from both and MUST give them one type, because the two differ only in where the declaration is made.
A release MUST refuse a status that is not a whole number from 200 to 599 at the call that declares it, with `invalid-configuration`.

A routing outcome carries the fact and not the status: a release MUST take the absence of an entity and its permanent removal as facts and MUST derive the status from the table above, because the table above is the release's and an application writing a status into a declaration would be restating a rule the release already applies.

A release MUST accept a declaration as a result distinct from the response a renderer otherwise returns, so a renderer that returns an ordinary response is unaffected and no status arrives as a declaration by accident.
A release MUST NOT read a status a renderer did not declare as a declaration, because an accidental failure and a deliberate one arriving as the same value cannot be told apart.

A release MUST send the document a declaration carries as the renderer gave it, with the status, the classification, and the indexing of the declared outcome on the response, and MUST NOT write into that document.

A release MUST carry it from the render to the response over a channel the two already share, MUST NOT carry it in a header or anywhere else a client can write or a response can expose, and MUST treat a render that declared nothing as the address's own outcome rather than as a declaration of success.

Where the render and the handler do not share that channel there is no declaration to read, and a release MUST report that during development rather than answer from the table as though the page had said nothing, because the two produce the same response and only the first is a wiring fault.

A release MUST NOT let a declaration reach a second render at the same address, a second navigation, or a second request, which is the rule section 2 already states for a parameter-spelling declaration and holds here for the same reason.

Where the two can disagree the narrower rule holds: a release MUST carry a declaration where the address resolved to a route it serves, and MUST send the status the table above gives wherever the address resolved to anything else, because a consumer application declaring an outcome cannot know which addresses the release answered from the table, and a rule it cannot reason about is not one it can apply.

A release MUST report a declaration it did not carry where a developer will see it during development, naming the address, what was declared, and what was sent, and MUST NOT report it more than once for one such pair, because the addresses it can arrive at are unbounded and supplied by the request.
A carried operational failure is not the address's representation, so a release MUST classify the response carrying it as private and not stored, whatever the address's own classification is.
A declaration has no response to reach on a client navigation, and a release MUST NOT synthesize one.
A release MUST fail the build for either and MUST NOT write the page.

A page declares once its own work settles, after the application has started, so a release MUST end that render as one that failed rather than only refuse the call that declared: the render otherwise goes on to write whatever is on screen.
A release MUST build a locale-entry redirect's destination in the locale it resolved to, so the redirect lands on a canonical URL in one hop.
An address that already states its locale is authoritative, and a release MUST NOT let a resolved preference override it.

A release MUST classify an entry redirect as private and revalidated before every reuse whether or not a preference was consulted, because marking either answer publicly cacheable lets a shared cache hand one visitor's language to the next, and marking the other private prevents nothing once the first is held under the same key.

Under a locale-neutral policy an address more than one locale spells states no locale, so a release MUST classify a successful response there as varying by locale preference, including a response that consulted nothing, because it shares a key with one that did.
A release MUST NOT classify a redirect produced under that policy as varying, because what a redirect returns is its location and that is the same for every locale.
A consumer application MUST declare that source.

A release MUST classify that response as private and revalidated before every reuse, for the reason an entry redirect is: a browser may keep it, and asks the server again before using it, so a visitor who has chosen another language since is answered in it.

A page a browser restores from its back-forward cache is the one reuse that does not ask the server, so a release that classifies a cookie-derived response as revalidated MUST check a restored page on the client: where the persisted locale differs from the locale on screen, and the configured sources would choose it at the address the page is at, the page changes to it.

A release MUST name the request language header in `Vary` on every response whose locale a preference read from that header chose, including a locale-entry redirect, a private response, and a declared outcome at such an address, because the field also tells a browser the answer was negotiated.
A release MUST NOT name a cookie in `Vary`.

A release MUST resolve it to the canonical route and render it in the committed locale, and MUST report the call in development, naming the address as written, the canonical address, and the operation that does change locale.
A release MUST commit the locale, yield no route context, and supply no body of its own, because which page answers a missing address belongs to the application.

A release MUST write the head of a response at such an address under section 12: a response whose title is empty and whose description belongs to whichever page was on screen before it fails the coherence requirement of section 15.

A release MUST answer with 308 only where strict parsing proves the request is a user-independent one-to-one variant of one final canonical URL, and MUST combine compatible host, locale, static-segment, slash, alias, and query corrections into a single hop.

A release MUST NOT case-fold a dynamic identity, and MUST NOT rewrite one except through its codec, a declared mapping, or the normalization to Form C stated below, which a parameter is given before its codec reads it.

A release MUST report the locale and the route that the location resolves to for the same request, including under a locale-neutral policy where two locales read the corrected spelling as two different routes.

Where the internal address it is handed is such a variant, a parameter spelled as another locale spells it among them, a release MUST write the canonical address the correction names rather than the variant, because the variant is an address the release then answers with a correction or, where the locale is in the host, with a not-found.
A client navigation to such a variant MUST arrive at the canonical address in place of the variant's history entry, so the page reads the parameters a document request for the same address reads.
A release MUST answer it with a 308 to that address, keeping the query, and MUST answer it as not found where two locales' spellings name two different addresses.
A release MUST NOT copy raw URL text, and MUST NOT let a query or fragment value choose an origin, an executable destination, a catalog identity, or a trust decision.

A release MUST read either one there, written as itself or escaped, and MUST write both as themselves in the canonical address, so a return address such as `?next=/account` is the same text after a canonical correction or a redirect as before it.

A release MUST read each decoded path segment, query name, query value, and fragment in that form, a parameter before its codec reads it, and MUST answer a spelling that is not in it as a variant of the one that is.

A bounded typed query value joins canonical identity only where a route declares a stable indexable representation, and a release MUST NOT promote accepted transient query state into cache, telemetry, or indexing identity on its own.

A release MUST commit a locale transaction and let the address bar follow it, leaving the route, its parameters, and its history entry unchanged by the switch itself, and a consumer application MUST change locale through the localization API rather than by navigating to a localized address.

Where the route on screen has no address in the target locale, because a parameter has no spelling there or because a declared spelling is one the route's codec refuses, a release MUST end the change as failed with the diagnostic the address was refused with, MUST NOT commit a locale the address bar cannot follow, and MUST NOT send the document to another origin.
A release MUST answer a change made in place while a navigation is in flight for the route on screen, as it answers any other, because that navigation can still be cancelled.

Where that navigation has already committed its locale and has not landed, a release MUST answer the change for the navigation's destination as well, and MUST write the page that lands in the locale that is committed.

Where that change does not commit, a release MUST fail the navigation with the diagnostic the change ended with, or with `route-unavailable` where the change ended as redirected and carries none, and MUST leave the snapshot and the Router's address as they were.

Where that navigation is cancelled or fails instead, or lands and the writing of its document throws, a release MUST put back the page it left in the locale the change committed, and MUST NOT put back the locale from before the navigation, because the change committed and its caller was told so.
A release MUST publish a snapshot only through a transaction, including when a single scope finishes loading, so every commit observer sees the same kind of event.

A release MUST publish the configured locales as options carrying the tag, the bare language subtag, the writing direction, the locale's own name in its own language, and whether it is current or arriving, MUST write the option's language, direction, and current state onto the control the application binds, and MUST render no markup of its own.
A consumer application writes the loop and the markup, and MUST NOT spell a locale out in a template.

An Equator release MUST NOT read it from the host's own display-name implementation where the pinned release has one, because the engines disagree: over sixteen locales on the four engines a release gates on, three differed, and a server-rendered label then changed under the visitor on hydration.
A release MUST derive the per-locale path of the resolved route once per navigation and publish it, and MUST form the head's alternate cluster and a switcher option's address from that one value.
A release MUST write that address to the link's own address attribute and to nothing else.

A release MUST replace the current entry for a canonical correction, MUST NOT change the address or persistence on a failed or superseded commit, and MUST confine a progressive region's failure to that region.

entries.section: 8. Scroll and focus across a direction change
entries.statement: A locale switch that changes the document's reading direction MUST preserve the visitor's logical scroll position on both axes, and a release is what preserves it.

entries.section: 8. Scroll and focus across a direction change
entries.statement: A release MUST capture the logical distance from the inline start before the commit and restore it re-signed for the direction the document is in afterwards, in the same frame that restores focus and selection.

entries.section: 8. Scroll and focus across a direction change
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT read the document's scroll range at capture or at restore, because a scroll call clamps to the range on its own and a document that has not finished growing then costs the visitor accuracy rather than correctness.

entries.section: 8. Scroll and focus across a direction change
entries.statement: Writing the position once is therefore not enough, so a release MUST hold it: for a bounded window after the restore, a viewport movement the runtime did not request and the visitor did not make is undone by re-applying the captured position.

entries.section: 8. Scroll and focus across a direction change
entries.statement: Six bounds close that window, and a release MUST apply all six.

entries.section: 8. Scroll and focus across a direction change
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT restore a position an application sets for itself afterwards, and a consumer application setting one should expect to be working against scroll anchoring on a document just relaid out in the opposite direction.
Render mode stays the application's declaration, because it is a decision about freshness and authorization, and a release MUST relay the framework's own render mode values without interpreting them.
A release MUST derive that expansion from the route projection and the narrowed policy, so a consumer application states a route's render mode once rather than once per locale.

A release MUST check the route identities in those declarations against the projection rather than accept free strings, and MUST NOT reach for a non-public framework token to read the policy and the projection from injection, because the server table is built at module scope before any injector exists and the framework's installer takes a concrete table at call time.
A release MUST fail the build for a value with no representation in some locale rather than omit it, because omitting it ships a page that exists in one language and is missing in another.
A release MUST fail the build the same way for a value whose spelling in some locale is not one safe path segment, because the build writes a file at the address that spelling completes.
A release MUST accept the values from a function the build calls as well as from a set written in place, and MUST serialize both the same way.
A consumer application's host MUST resolve a request for a directory to the index document inside it, matching on the decoded path.
entries.reason: This binds the static host a consumer application deploys to; the release writes the prerendered files and has no part in how a host maps a directory request to them.

entries.statement: Where a release is itself the host, it MUST decode before lookup.
entries.reason: No published package serves prerendered files: the request handler renders or passes through, and the only file server in the tree is the gate's own test server, which is not part of a release.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT force prerendering onto a route whose existence, authorization, or freshness cannot be proven at build time.

A release MUST fail the build when it renders a route whose level under section 16 is per visitor or not stored, or whose indexing class is private, and MUST NOT write the page, whichever declaration led the build to render it: an entry of its own, a fallback, or an application shell.

It MUST decide this from the route's classification and from the render having no request, and MUST NOT read a render mode value to decide it, because this section relays those values without interpreting them.
entries.reason: The refusal in the router provider is never handed a render mode value, so there is nothing it could read; the half about the render having no request is exercised only by the refused prerender builds that statement 93 names.

entries.statement: Under a locale-neutral policy an address more than one locale spells has no locale until a request states a preference, so it is per visitor whatever its route declares, and a release MUST refuse to prerender it the same way.

A release MUST compose every URL it publishes or writes into a document from those three and nothing else, so the address a crawler is given and the address this build resolves are two readings of one fact.
A release MUST therefore refuse at configuration a server render that has not been told its origin, under every policy.
A release MUST require all three, because none implies another and an alternate link is a public claim that the same page exists in another language.

A release MAY advertise a locale-neutral entry resolver as the unmatched-visitor default only where it deterministically resolves visitors into the localized cluster without serving a competing localized representation.
entries.reason: It grants a permission: a release that never advertises such a resolver as the default complies, so there is no behavior to withdraw.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT emit a canonical or alternate cluster for an unsupported-locale, malformed, missing, gone, private, or otherwise non-indexable response.
A release MUST produce the complete file set with each file's name, contents, kind, URL count, and size, and a consumer application writes or serves it and states the sitemap line in its robots file.

A release MUST split a set on both of the protocol's limits, fifty thousand URLs and fifty megabytes uncompressed measured in the bytes served, because with a reciprocal alternate cluster in every entry the size limit is reached before the count.

A release MUST emit a last-modified value only from a value a route declares, and MUST NOT derive one from a build time or a file time, because it is the one optional element a search engine reads and it reads it only where it can be verified.
A release MUST validate the files against the published schemas, pinned alongside the other normative data.
A release MUST read all three, MUST apply them in that order with a later field replacing an earlier one, and MUST NOT require a consumer application to supply a field at more than one of them.

A release MUST resolve a declared message with the inputs declared beside it, MUST refuse a declaration naming a message that takes inputs with none bound to it, and MUST refuse it where the declaration is built rather than where the page is visited.
