A release MUST re-project the document when one arrives rather than leave the head as it was built, MUST stamp it with the navigation that made it, MUST replace a committed declaration outright when a navigation commits, including when the arriving page declares nothing, and MUST discard the declaration of a navigation that was cancelled.

A release MUST remove everything it wrote for the previous document before writing the next, so no head carries a mixture of two pages, and MUST NOT require a consumer application to clear a field by declaring it empty.

A release MUST recompute them after a declaration and MUST NOT leave a canonical or an alternate standing on a response the page has declared absent or removed, because an alternate link is a public claim that the same page exists in another language and section 10 already forbids one on a missing or gone response.
An indexing class may be narrowed by a declaration and MUST NOT be widened by one.

A page may declare that it is not to be indexed today; it MUST NOT declare itself indexable where the route's own class under section 14 says otherwise, because that class is a property of the address and a page that could raise it could publish an address the application withheld.

A release MUST read those declarations for a response of the matching class, MUST author them as messages so that catalog completeness answers for them under the same diagnostic as every other message rather than under a second mechanism, and MUST report a class with no declaration when a response of that class is answered, because the response is otherwise served with no title.

A release supplies the localized title and description, the canonical URL, and the locale identity with its eligible alternates, and MUST emit no social block until the application has supplied an image, because the format requires one.

A release MUST write the social locale in the underscore form that format specifies rather than the language tag used elsewhere in the document, MUST resolve the territory from the maximized locale profile where the format is silent, MUST omit a script subtag the format has nowhere to put, and MUST emit no locale value at all when no territory can be determined, because a consumer of the markup cannot distinguish a malformed value from an unrecognized territory.
A release MUST NOT list a page's own locale among its social alternates.
A release MUST emit a card tag only where the card format has no Open Graph equivalent, because the card processor falls back to Open Graph.

A release MUST read a field name it was given rather than one of its own invention, MUST treat a value the declaration does not list as indexable, and MUST supply a documented default field for a project that declares none.

A release MUST read that declaration from the provider file's source text when the owner is compiled, and MUST NOT execute consumer code to obtain it, which is why the declaration is a field name and a table of literals rather than a predicate.

A literal MAY be written in place or through a `const` binding to one, in the same file or imported, and a release MUST follow the binding without evaluating anything, as section 5 of `10-compiler-and-tooling.spec.md` follows a constant alias.
The same holds for a route's data: a field MAY arrive through such a binding or a spread of one, and a later key overrides an earlier one as it does when the application runs.

A value it could not read, because it is computed, a parameter, supplied by a resolver, or behind a binding it cannot follow, is not an unlisted value, and a release MUST answer the route as private and report it when the owner is compiled.

The data a route has when the application runs is its own over what it inherits from its parents, and a release MUST read declarations the same way, so a class declared on a parent reaches every child the framework gives it to.

A release MUST apply the framework's rule: a child inherits when the router inherits always, when the child's own path is empty, or when its parent renders no component, and a key of the child's own wins.
A release MUST read the router's inheritance strategy from the application's router configuration and use the framework's default, which is to inherit always, where none is declared.

Where the strategy cannot be read, or is declared more than once, a release MUST report it and inherit always, because for the indexing and caching classes inheriting can only give a child that states nothing its parent's class, which never makes a page more shareable or more indexable than its routes say.
Where the framework decides it at run time, through a matcher or a guard, a release MUST answer the address as private and not-stored and report it, as it does a value it cannot read.
A release MUST refuse a value the protocol would reject when the owner is compiled rather than drop it, because a silently omitted claim turns a mistyped one into a page that says nothing.
A release MUST emit a non-indexable directive through both the server-rendered metadata and the HTTP header where the host integration supports both.

A robots directive is defense in depth and MUST NOT be relied on by a consumer application as authentication or confidentiality, and a robots file does not replace it, canonicalization, or authorization.
entries.reason: It binds how a consumer application protects its pages; a release emits the directive and has no way to see whether an application also authorizes the request.

entries.statement: A release MAY render an unsupported-locale response in a last known supported presentation locale while stating that the requested locale was not activated.
entries.reason: It grants a permission: rendering the response in the default locale, as the router does today, complies as well, so there is no behavior to withdraw.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT mutate locale persistence, advertise the unsupported locale, or reflect arbitrary path values into links on one.

An ordinary missing route under a supported locale uses that locale for the root language and direction, the accessible content, the title, and any trusted recovery destination, and a release MUST keep it a 404 rather than redirect to a homepage or a guessed route.

A release MUST hand a renderer the locale the response's content language names: the resolved locale at a page, the locale a prefix or an origin states at a missing or removed page under it, the negotiated locale at a missing locale-neutral address, and the default locale at an address under a prefix policy that states no locale the policy serves.
An unknown unprefixed route is a direct 404 rather than a locale negotiation, and a release MUST emit no canonical or alternate relationship for it.
A release MUST preserve each region's actual language, direction, readiness, and outcome rather than relabel it as the primary locale.
A human-language field uses its message result or its participant result, and a release MUST NOT admit a consumer payload into the localization snapshot.

A release MUST take canonical origins and redirect targets from trusted configuration rather than from a request-controlled host or header, and MUST NOT let a locale switch create an open redirect, host injection, cache poisoning, provider crossover, or leakage between request contexts.

A release MUST emit the cache directives it fully determines and MUST take the durations it cannot choose as arguments, because whether a shared cache may hold a response is a conclusion about a release's own routing while how long to hold it is a number a release has no basis to pick.

A release MUST express what it emits as a set of headers by name rather than one header's text, so an application writes the set with one loop and gains a header a later release adds without changing a line.

A release computes a level for each response from its routing classification, and MUST let each declaration below raise that level and none lower it, because a declaration that could lower it could publish a page that its route or its host said must not be shared.

A release MUST answer a value it cannot read, or reads and cannot use, as not stored, and MUST report it when the owner is compiled, because every value the declaration can name keeps the page out of a shared cache, and reading an unusable one as absent is the one reading that cannot be what was meant.
A release MUST apply it to every response that carries a page, and MUST NOT apply it to a redirect, which carries none.

A page's own cache directives are the third declaration, and a release MUST combine them with its own rather than replace them, narrowing only: a page knows what it put in itself and cannot know which other responses share its address.
A release MUST NOT carry a directive that lengthens or widens reuse, and MUST read a lifetime given twice or not as a whole number as stale, as RFC 9111 section 4.2.1 offers.

A release MUST read every directive the page's value spells, including one that follows another with no comma between them, so a value written `max-age=60 no-store` is not stored, because RFC 9111 section 5.2.2.5 has that directive forbid storing any part of the response.
A release MUST add the page's varying fields to its own, except a cookie, which raises the page to per visitor instead, and a wildcard, which stands alone.
A release MUST store, transport, compare, cache, validate, and identify a domain value in locale-invariant form.

A localized string is presentation output, and a release MUST NOT let one become authoritative money, a number, a date or time, a duration, a unit, an enum, a route, a cache key, an authorization value, or a protocol field.
A consumer application's own user, organization, tenant, route, field, or operation policy decides their precedence, and a release MUST NOT take any of them from the host machine's ambient settings.

A release MUST normalize and validate these through public factories, and MUST admit a platform date, a native temporal value, a transport object, a decimal library value, or a domain-library value only through an explicit adapter that cannot confuse seconds with milliseconds, civil time with an instant, a currency, a precision, or a unit.

A release MUST take time-zone identity, aliases, and links from the pinned time-zone database recorded under `01-standards-profile.spec.md` section 4, and MUST NOT let host presentation data redefine a stored time-zone identity.

A time zone's identity MUST be the primary identifier the pinned database gives its name, as ECMA-402 section 6.5 defines one: a Zone is primary, a Link resolves to the Zone it names, a Link that the `TZ` column of `zone.tab` lists is primary itself, any other Link whose Zone lies in another country resolves to a name `zone.tab` lists for the Link's own country, and `Etc/UTC`, `Etc/GMT`, `GMT` and their Links are `UTC`.

A release MUST resolve a name the database added to replace a Zone, where the database keeps the former name as a Link, to that former name until the pinned release is two years or more later than the release that renamed it, the waiting period section 6.5.1 of that standard recommends, because an identifier stored earlier is one a system on older data cannot read.

A release MUST format a plain date or date-time counted in `gregory`, which is what a date field of that calendar reads, and MUST write it in the Gregorian calendar, under the calendar an operation names and over the context's.
A release MUST NOT perform accounting, exchange, tax, cash rounding, business precision, rate calculation, percentage-point conversion, or implicit unit conversion.
entries.reason: It excludes capabilities the runtime does not have, so there is no behavior to remove and see a test fail. The nearest observable property, that formatting reports rather than rounds an exact decimal it cannot represent, is its own statement elsewhere.

entries.statement: A release MUST feature-detect a capability before relying on it, and MUST return a typed unsupported result, or use an explicitly installed adapter, where required behavior is absent or inconsistent.
A release MUST NOT approximate one silently.

A release MUST accept an instant at whatever precision it carries and format it to the precision the requested options ask for, and MUST reserve a refusal for output that was genuinely requested and cannot be produced, which no date-time option expresses below a millisecond.

Localized output is identical across every runtime in the supported envelope, except where a supported runtime lacks a capability: that runtime returns the typed unsupported result above, and a release MUST name the capability and the runtime in its documentation.

A release MUST format real content in each supported locale on each supported runtime and compare the results, because a browser and a server that render the same page must not produce different text.

A release MUST use one immutable formatting snapshot across server rendering, hydration, and browser evaluation, so hydrated output matches the server exactly, and MUST take an explicit reference instant or clock for a clock-sensitive operation.
A release MUST NOT conflate the two.
A release MUST use the declared semantic scale when formatting a percent.
Percentage points are a separate contract and a release MUST NOT let one enter percent formatting implicitly.
A release MUST NOT let a narrow per-operation override mutate global state.
Structured parts preserve the semantic kind, the source value identity where that is safe, and the language and direction metadata, and a release MUST NOT put trusted markup in one.
A release MUST key a cached formatter on its complete locale and options identity and MUST bound that cache, so arbitrary option cardinality cannot grow memory without limit.

The options of one operation, a formatting call or a message expression, are narrower than all three, and a release MUST format with the time zone, calendar, or hour cycle an operation names over the context's.

A release MUST refuse a calendar that is not written as section 2 writes a calendar's name without asking the host, and MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3 from every date formatter where the host answers a well-formed name with another calendar, which a host does without an error for a calendar it does not have and for an alias of one it has.

A release MUST format with the numbering system an operation names over the context's, MUST refuse one that is not written as UTS #35 Part 1 writes the type of a numbering system, one or more subtags of three to eight lower-case ASCII letters and digits joined by hyphens, without asking the host, and MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3 from every formatter that writes digits where the host has no digits under a well-formed name, which a host given the name does not report.

A release MUST refuse a collation that is not written as the type of a collation is, the same syntax, without asking the host, and MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3 where the host answers a well-formed name with another collation, which a host does without an error for a collation it does not have and for one the locale does not have.

A release MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3, with the reason `native-capability-rejected`, from every date formatter and every message function that writes a date where the host does not read the name it is given as a zone, and MUST NOT write the date in another zone.

An hour cycle the context names is judged by the host the same way, and a release MUST return the same typed unsupported result from every date formatter and every message function where the host does not read it.

A plain time or date-time has no zone and is written at its own fields, which writing it in UTC does, so a release MUST write it under a zone an operation names where the host reads that zone as UTC, whatever name the zone is given there, and MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3 under any other zone.
A release MUST fall back the same way on every host, through the pinned parent chain of `03-locale-identity-and-resolution.spec.md` section 4 to the first locale the host has for the operation.

A release MUST walk the chain of the component the operation's data comes from: plural selection the plurals component, ordering the collations component, segmentation the segmentations component, and every other operation the main one, so `sr-Latn` takes the plural rules of `sr` while its numbers inherit from root.

A release MUST report a fallback, as `fallback` on the first two and `valueFallback` on the third, where that locale differs from the context's in language or in script, and MUST NOT report one where it differs in neither: `en` answering for `en-US` is not a fallback, and `fr-HT` writing for `ht` and `zh` answering for `zh-TW` are.

The chain ends at root, which writes no language, and a release MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3, with the reason `native-capability-rejected`, where no locale of the chain is one the host has.

A keyword of the context's locale that the operation reads, `ca`, `hc` or `nu` for a date, `nu` for a number, a relative time or a duration, and `co`, `kf` or `kn` for an ordering, goes with the locale that formats, and a release MUST report one the host drops as it reports an option the host drops.
A release MUST let a locale declare only what is a fact about how it is written: its numbering system, its calendar, and its hour cycle.

A time zone is not one of those, so a release MUST keep the time zone application-wide, because it belongs to the reader or the deployment rather than to the language, and one page is read in one zone whichever language it is in.
A release MUST NOT let it become the default for another locale.

A release MUST walk the chain of a context so marked without the likely-script rule, as `03-locale-identity-and-resolution.spec.md` section 4 states, and MUST take the context's script to be the likely script of its language, so `en-Arab-XB` is written as `en` writes, in the digits its declaration names, and is not a fallback.

A release MUST return the typed unsupported result of section 3, with the reason `malformed-input`, from every operation that walks the chain where the member marks a locale whose region is not one a pseudo-locale takes.
Relative-time presentation is divided by owner, and a release MUST hold that division.

A consumer application owns the thresholds, declaring the smallest and largest units worth naming and the elapsed span past which relative phrasing stops, and MUST NOT implement unit selection itself.
entries.reason: It binds the consumer application's own code, and a release cannot see whether an application also selects units itself before calling a formatter. The release's half, providing selection so an application need not, is checked under statement 22.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT report it as a formatting failure and MUST NOT substitute an absolute rendering, because the format, the zone, and the wording of that rendering belong to the application.
A release MUST NOT expose a universal permissive parser.
entries.reason: It forbids adding an API rather than requiring a behavior, so there is nothing present to remove and watch a test fail. Every parser the release exposes takes a declared field profile, and the surface gates flag any new export without being able to tell a permissive parser from any other.

entries.statement: A result is one of valid, incomplete, invalid, ambiguous, out-of-range, unsupported-capability, or policy-rejected, and a release MUST carry an invariant typed value only on the valid one.
A release MAY preserve incomplete localized text during composition or editing.
entries.reason: It grants a permission, and no behavior of a release can violate a permission it is free not to use.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT, on commit, select the first plausible interpretation, change a currency or a unit, or resolve a daylight-saving ambiguity silently.

A release MUST reverse the field's declared scale when parsing a percent, so localized twenty-five percent yields a quarter under fractional semantics and twenty-five under a declared percent-unit profile.
A release MUST NOT use the platform's permissive date parser, host coercion, a guessed field order, natural-language guessing, or the host's implicit time zone as a correctness path.
A release MUST NOT locale-parse a domain code, an enum value, an identifier, a route or cache key, an authorization value, a protocol field, or a machine timestamp.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: Locale-aware collation and case conversion are presentation and search aids, and a release MUST NOT use either for a security decision or an identity comparison.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: A release MUST preserve the fields supplied, MUST distinguish the name's own language and script from the surrounding locale, MUST NOT impose a universal given-and-family persistence schema, and MUST NOT parse an unstructured name into authoritative components.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: A release localizes the labels, the instructions, and the issue presentation around them, and MUST NOT define an address or telephone database, validator, or provider contract.
entries.reason: It excludes capabilities the release does not have, so there is no behavior to remove and see a test fail.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: A release MUST resolve the adapter through the calling context's own registry, MUST apply the descriptor's input bound before invoking it, MUST supply the committed formatting snapshot, and MUST refuse a generated required descriptor whose trusted binding is absent or not byte-for-byte compatible.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: An extension MUST run synchronously and return bounded text or coherent structured parts.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: A release MUST return an explicit unsupported-formatting result for a handler that is missing, asynchronous, throwing, malformed, or over its bound, and MUST take a parsing adapter's result type from the adapter rather than from the caller, because a caller-declared result type is an assertion nothing checks.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: An extension MUST NOT weaken the strict result model or reach a consumer that did not select it.

entries.section: 7. Locale data, person names, and what stays domain-owned
entries.statement: A release MUST format such a name rather than throw: a monogram is the first code point of its field, and a field a pattern asks for in capitals takes the case mapping that belongs to no locale.
The core behavior works without a Forms adapter, and a release MUST keep an optional Forms value import out of the primary entry point, under `02-packages-and-platform.spec.md` section 6.
A release MUST give it a safe generic presentation and a diagnostic, MUST NOT reject the transport merely because a code is unknown, and MUST NOT coerce it into a known value.
A release MUST NOT restrict localized input to one element type where the form system binds a value accessor to more than one.

A release MUST hold such a write until it can be honoured rather than fail on it, and MUST NOT require a consumer application to discover the ordering and buffer around it, because the order of the two bindings is the framework's rather than the application's.

A release MUST update the wording on a locale change while preserving the control value, the selection, the composition, the dirty, touched, and pending state, the validation result, and the parameters.
A release maps it to a localized message in the active context, and MUST NOT call or control the originating system.
entries.reason: It excludes a capability the issue path does not have: presentation takes a code and a message group and returns text, with nothing to call. There is no behavior to remove and see a test fail.

entries.statement: A release MUST read a code as a sequence of words and write them back as one lower-kebab message identifier, so the same failure reaches the same message whichever casing or separator convention the originating system uses, and a service that changes how it spells its codes does not orphan an application's translations.

A release MUST read every other character as a separator, a letter outside ASCII included, and MUST read the code as it is given, with no Unicode normalization, because a message identifier is written in ASCII letters and digits alone.

A release MUST NOT require a mapping line per code, because that is a line every new code needs and eventually does not get, and what the reader then sees is a generic apology instead of what went wrong.
An explicit binding stays available for what a convention cannot express, a code whose message lives elsewhere or several codes deliberately collapsing to one, and a release MUST consult it first.

A release MUST accept a message found by name only when the message's own identity ends in the derived identifier, because a message group is an ordinary value and the wrong one can be supplied, and rendering a message about something else is worse than rendering the generic one.

A release MUST treat a reference to a message group as a reference to every message in it, where the group is handed to something, and MUST NOT count walking through a group to reach a single message or importing it, because counting either would silence the unused-message advisory for every scope any file imports.
A release MUST NOT let localization reinterpret a failure as a success, weaken authorization or validation, or replace the application's own policy.

An unknown external value stays a typed unknown state and maps to a safe fallback with a diagnostic, and a release MUST keep machine equality and persistence on the invariant value rather than the localized label.

A release MUST NOT call or couple itself to a consumer content system, translation system, API, backend, database, vendor library, or data service, and MUST NOT let a consumer payload become a message identifier, compiled data, a cache entry, or part of a localization snapshot.
A release MUST keep the three apart.
A release MUST preserve its known or unknown actual language and direction and MUST NOT relabel it as fallback merely because it differs from the target locale.

entries.section: 11. Renderers the runtime does not own
entries.statement: The recipient's locale, time zone, formatting policy, content, authorization, retries, delivery, and audit behavior sit outside the Angular runtime, and a release MUST NOT call, host, or govern such a renderer.
entries.reason: It excludes a capability the runtime does not have: there is no renderer integration to remove and see a test fail.

entries.section: 11. Renderers the runtime does not own
entries.statement: Logs, metrics, analytics, security events, and protocol fields use invariant codes and structured values, and a release MUST NOT put localized text in one.

A release MUST treat authored and translated content as untrusted input, including content stored in a repository the consumer application controls, because a translation arrives through people and tools that the repository's permissions say nothing about.
Build trust follows bounded parsing and complete validation, and a release MUST NOT extend it to content that has not passed both.
A catalog MUST NOT acquire that authority by any route, and a release MUST NOT offer one.

A release MUST NOT let it execute JavaScript or WebAssembly, import code, request dependency injection, compile a template, instantiate a component or a directive, reach the DOM, the filesystem, the network, the process, storage, or a global, or produce an event handler, a callback, a style, a class, a permission, a sanitizer, a trusted value, or an executable expression.

A release MUST NOT use `eval`, the `Function` constructor, string-to-template compilation, or any equivalent runtime code generation on any path, so a strict content security policy costs a consumer application nothing to adopt.
A release MUST NOT treat that text as HTML, a URL, a style, a class, a DOM property, or a browser trusted value, and MUST NOT provide an interface that hands it to one.

A release MUST require a binding for each slot the parts carry and MUST refuse the message where a binding is absent or of the wrong kind: a `link` slot takes a link binding, an `action` slot takes an action binding, and any other slot takes a template or a text binding.
A release MUST NOT let a catalog choose a URL, an origin, a scheme, a target, a link relationship, a callback, a command, or an event.

A release MUST refuse the call for an entry that is anything else, whatever the other entries allow, and that refusal carries the reason `malformed-input`, so a caller can tell a list that was written wrongly from an address the list does not hold.
An address that is not text is a call written wrongly, for a destination on another site and for one inside the application alike, and a release MUST refuse it with the reason `malformed-input`.
A release MUST admit an address only when it is HTTPS at one of those origins and carries no credentials.
A release MUST preserve localized text, formatted values, and the children of a container slot in that projection, and MUST NOT let a destination, a handler, or protected binding data appear in it.
That covers color, emphasis, a design-system component, or a purpose-built one, and a release MUST NOT let a catalog choose CSS, a class, a color, a design token, a component, or behavior.
A release MUST NOT provide a catalog-addressable component registry, because a catalog that can name a component can name any component in the application.
Arbitrary HTML is not a message surface, and a release MUST NOT accept one in a catalog.

Where a legacy corpus makes an adapter necessary, that adapter MUST be explicit and isolated, MUST use a separately approved parser and sanitizer with a closed allowlist, MUST produce safe semantic output, and MUST preserve Angular sanitization, the content security policy, Trusted Types, server rendering, hydration, and accessibility.
entries.reason: A release ships no HTML adapter, so these requirements bind whoever writes one for a legacy corpus. There is no adapter code in either package whose behavior a check could withdraw.

entries.statement: An adapter MUST NOT weaken the text and parts contracts and MUST NOT turn remote content into an executable template.
entries.reason: This constrains an HTML adapter, which no release ships; the text and parts contracts it must not weaken are proven by the checks on those contracts themselves.

entries.section: 6. Content security policy and Trusted Types
entries.statement: A release MUST operate with no inline script, no unsafe evaluation, no sanitizer bypass, no permissive Trusted Types policy, and no runtime template compilation, under a policy that denies everything by default and allows script only from the application's own origin and its inline hashes, denies attribute-position script, denies plugin content, and requires Trusted Types for script.

entries.section: 6. Content security policy and Trusted Types
entries.statement: A release MUST keep the ordinary text and structured-parts paths free of that dependency, so an application that does not enable the integration inherits none of it.

A release MUST parse YAML, JSON, XML and XLIFF, MessageFormat, and local manifests with bounded non-executing parsers, MUST NOT let a parsed document trigger filesystem or network resolution, and MUST refuse a document type declaration and an external entity in XLIFF.

A release MUST validate Unicode scalar structure wherever text becomes an identity, refusing an unpaired surrogate and a noncharacter, and MUST refuse a control character that no interface text contains.
A release MUST refuse a confusable structural token or a control capable of spoofing a source file, a route, a diagnostic, or generated code.
A release MUST refuse an authored catalog value that contains any of the following.
A release MUST accept a balanced directional isolate, which contains a direction instead of leaking it and is what a translator needs around a left-to-right product name inside right-to-left prose.

A release MUST accept a directional mark (U+200E, U+200F, U+061C), which affects one adjacent character and cannot reorder a run, and the zero-width space and word joiner (U+200B, U+2060), which have ordinary typographic uses.
A release MUST say what the refused character does rather than only that one was found, because the reader cannot see it.
An interpolated value can reposition the text around it, so a release MUST isolate it in the formatter rather than leave each call site to remember.
A release MUST NOT make one of those surfaces weaker than the other, because choosing a rendering surface is not a choice about safety.

A release MUST isolate a right-to-left value in either direction of message, MUST isolate a value of unknown direction with a first-strong isolate so the renderer's own rule decides, and MUST isolate a left-to-right value in a right-to-left message.

It MUST NOT isolate a left-to-right value in a left-to-right message unless the author asked for it, because the characters are invisible to a reader and visible to every string comparison a consumer application writes, and inserting them where they change nothing costs those comparisons and buys nothing.

For a value the runtime did not format, a release has no locale to take a direction from, so it MAY read the value's own content to decide, and MUST accept an explicit author declaration in its place.
A release MUST NOT write a directional control into a stored value or return one from a value contract.
Every user-facing primitive a release supplies, and every reference integration it ships, MUST conform to WCAG 2.2 level AA for the behavior it implements.
A release MUST provide a way to place a message in attribute position directly, and MUST restrict it to a closed set of attributes whose value is presented rather than fetched, executed, or resolved.

A release MUST refuse an attribute outside that set, because `href`, `src`, `formaction`, and every event attribute are positions where a string stops being text and becomes a navigation or a program, and routing translated content into one of them MUST NOT be a one-word template change.
A release MUST write the named attribute alone and leave every other attribute as the author wrote it.
A target catalog MUST NOT cause a required semantic action to disappear, and a release MUST refuse the message rather than render an interface that has lost one.

In its Angular integration, a release MUST keep the document element's language and direction, and the declared localized head metadata, in step with the committed snapshot across server rendering, hydration, and every transition, without being asked, because a page whose text is Arabic and whose direction is left to right is broken in a way no application intends.
A consumer application that does not own the document MAY withdraw that, and a release MUST make the withdrawal an explicit statement rather than a flag whose other value changes nothing.

A release MUST give a fallback segment, a quotation, a name, a formatted external value, and any other change of language explicit language and direction metadata, so a renderer can scope the language and isolate the run.

A release MUST report an undetermined tag with no script subtag, and an absent tag, as unknown and defer the direction to the renderer's first-strong rule; MUST report a tag that carries no linguistic content as language-independent and defer in the same way; and MUST NOT assign a writing direction to either.
A release exposes direction signals, logical direction tokens, diagnostics, and optional static checks, and MUST NOT rewrite a consumer application's CSS.
A consumer application SHOULD write logical CSS properties and MUST classify a genuinely physical direction explicitly.
entries.reason: This binds the consumer application's own stylesheets and icon classification. A release reads none of that CSS, so there is no release behavior a check could withdraw.

entries.statement: A release MUST therefore announce a locale change without being asked, into a live region it owns, and MUST announce it only after the transition commits.
A consumer application MAY replace the wording, and a release MUST treat that as a replacement of the wording alone rather than of the decision to announce.

An application announcing the change through a region of its own supplies none, so the change is not announced twice, and a release MUST accept that rather than treat an empty replacement as a mistake.
A release MUST ask for the replacement wording once the change is published, so a wording read from the application's messages is in the locale arrived at.
Where the wording it gets cannot be announced, a release MUST report that and announce the default instead.
A release MUST NOT announce an entire page, a pending locale, a failed switch as a success, or every translated node.

Across a locale switch that stays on the same view, a release MUST preserve focus on the control that started it, where that control is still in the document and nothing else has taken focus in the meantime.

The restore is scheduled during the commit and applied a frame or more later, by which time a visitor may have pressed another control, tabbed away, or clicked into a field, so where anything other than the document body or the document element holds focus at that moment, somebody chose it, and a release MUST leave that choice alone.
A release MUST NOT mutate a form value, a selection, or an active text composition across the switch.

A selection offset is a position in a particular string, so a release MUST restore offsets only where the text they were measured against is unchanged, and a consumer application's component that rewrites its own value across the commit owns the mapping for that value.
A release MUST NOT move focus for a change of reading direction alone.
A release MUST NOT require a transition animation.
A consumer application's motion MUST honor a reduced-motion preference and MUST NOT delay correctness, focus, or the commit.
entries.reason: This binds the consumer application's own motion, which a release neither supplies nor runs.

entries.statement: A release MUST create that adapter once per injector rather than once per configuration, because under server rendering there is one injector per request and one application configuration for the process: an adapter created where the feature is declared is shared by every concurrent request, and the first request to finish disposes it for all of them.
A release MUST update a coordinated overlay's content and direction with the primary commit and MUST NOT leave one holding a mixed-locale state.

A release MAY let an overlay a consumer application declared progressive complete on its own, and only while that overlay reports truthful readiness, outcome, supplying language, and direction; its pending, replacement, and failure presentation stays the consumer application's.
entries.reason: The statement grants a permission, and the truthful reporting it is conditioned on is the consumer overlay's to supply; no release behavior violates a permission it may decline to use.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT select an overlay framework and MUST NOT add an overlay dependency to the primary entry point.
It MUST NOT bundle or download a font and MUST NOT rewrite a consumer application's design system.

A release MUST leave a direction-neutral icon, a physically directional one, a logo, media, a number, a culturally meaningful symbol, and an unclassified icon unchanged, because mirroring one of those produces an image that means something else.

An application's images, media, files, and documents are locale-neutral by default, and a release MUST NOT enroll one in a locale transition unless the application declared a localized variant for it.

A declared descriptor is neutral, variant-bearing, or fixed-language, and its source value is opaque trusted consumer data: a release MUST NOT construct, parse, or fetch it, and MUST NOT accept it from a catalog.
A release MUST NOT guess a fallback chain, and MUST return either a ready result naming the representation it selected and whether it fell back, or an unavailable result naming the exhausted policy.

A release MUST refuse one whose identity, locale, language, direction, variant list, fallback, representation, or status is not what its declaration allows, a value of another type where text or a list is declared included, with the typed `invalid-configuration` failure.

A government, legal, official, historical, registration, tax, certificate, or comparable authentic artifact preserves its original content and its actual language unless the authority behind it supplies a distinct localized variant, and a release MUST NOT treat authenticity as a missing translation.

A release MUST reconstruct a participant report from bounded status, outcome, identity, and representation metadata alone, and MUST NOT give that report a payload, a URL, an authorization, a storage, or a cache field.
An extension MUST NOT opt out of validation, resource limits, request isolation, the content security policy, accessibility, or transaction semantics, and a release MUST NOT provide a way to.

A release MUST resolve a binding through the calling context's own registry, so a binding belonging to another context or never installed in this one is refused, and MUST refuse a generated required descriptor whose trusted binding is absent or not byte-for-byte compatible.
A release MUST refuse a descriptor that is not inert data, whether a binding carries it or a catalog requires it, with the typed configuration failure it gives any other malformed descriptor.

A diagnostic about a security refusal MUST name a stable bounded cause category, and a release MUST NOT put a secret, a credential, a cookie, a token, a source or message body, a parameter, a slot payload, or unsafe text in one.
A release MUST NOT import, call, extend, or model itself around a consumer application's compiler, repository tool, build system, workspace layout, or project service.
A project-owned orchestrator MAY call either, and a release MUST NOT let one redefine compilation semantics or make the toolkit depend on the project.
entries.reason: The first half grants an orchestrator permission, which no release behavior can violate. The toolkit offers no hook through which a caller could change how compilation behaves, and that absence is not something a test run can observe; its dependency list is held by verify:packages under the statement before this one.

entries.statement: A release MUST make importing the toolkit start no compilation, no process mutation, no watch, and no filesystem write, so a build script that imports it to read one type pays for nothing else.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT give that core process state, networking, filesystem mutation, scheduling, or a watch lifecycle.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST route the command line and every integration through the same core, so an answer does not depend on which surface asked for it.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST treat only high-level requests, results, configuration, documented diagnostics, and generated public contracts as consumer-facing API.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST make a programmatic entry point that validates untrusted input accept an unknown value and confirm it is text within a bounded length before any grammar, coercion, or byte measurement reads it, and MUST report a value that is not text as a diagnostic naming the type received and never the value.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST throw a `TypeError` that names the function, the argument, and the type received and never the value when a programmatic entry point is called with an argument that is not its documented shape, and an asynchronous entry point rejects with that error.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST judge a catalog or a configuration that a caller assembles and hands to a programmatic entry point as `parseCatalog` and `parseConfiguration` judge the same content read from a file, and MUST report what they refuse with their diagnostics and no source position.

entries.section: 2. The compiler core and its hosts
entries.statement: A release MUST refuse an owner identity whose provider is outside the provider grammar with the diagnostic that provider gets in a catalog, whether or not the request carries a catalog.

A release MUST NOT read a TypeScript source that lies behind a link inside the owner, and MUST report it as a project diagnostic that names the source and the link by their paths relative to the owner.
A release MUST NOT write the provisional overlay, import it at run time, cache it as an authority, or expose it as a second generated interface.
A release MAY let existing generated files accelerate an equivalent incremental run once their completion manifest validates, and MUST NOT let them decide what a clean run produces.

A consumer application that deletes its generated root and its work root MUST be able to restore both with one successful generate, without commenting out an import, generating twice, checking in generated files, or writing a registry by hand.
A release MUST let each input class contribute only its own declared facts, and MUST NOT let one redefine catalog wording or message identity.
Every authored input is UTF-8 text, and a release MUST NOT decode one with replacement.

A release MUST refuse an authored input that is not UTF-8, or that exceeds its byte ceiling, with the code that input's other refusals carry and its path relative to the owner, and MUST NOT report either as an environment failure.
A release MUST read a JSON input that begins with a byte-order mark as the JSON after it (RFC 8259 section 8.1), and MUST keep the mark when it rewrites that file.

A release MUST NOT import or execute a handler, renderer, adapter, or application module to discover anything, and MUST validate a descriptor's schema, identity, namespace, profile, and fingerprint before it contributes a generated type or semantic-registry compatibility data.
An extension descriptor MUST NOT contain code or a fingerprint of its own, because the fingerprint is derived and a supplied one would be a claim nothing checked.
An absent file is an empty registry, and a release MUST NOT scaffold or require an empty one.
A release MUST fail with the candidates where more than one owner or configuration is plausible, and MUST NOT merge two projects because of the working directory.

Discovery is bounded by the package the working directory stands in: the nearest manifest upward, inclusive, is the project's root, and a release MUST NOT select a configuration above that boundary, and MUST name both the configuration it declined and the boundary it lies beyond.
A release MUST NOT take precedence from discovery order or path order, and MUST NOT accept a configured external or remote catalog source.

A release MUST exclude generated source, compiled catalogs, catalog-set descriptors, caches, reports, pseudo-locales, interchange documents, build output, declaration-only dependencies, ignored content, and unrelated projects unless an explicit supported local role says otherwise, and MUST fail deterministically on a complete catalog or message identity collision outside a declared compatible override layer.

A consumer application's pages, products, articles, comments, user-authored values, and other runtime domain records MUST NOT become a compiler input, a generated message contract, a reachability root, a catalog artifact, a cache entry, or output metadata, even where the application stores them locally.
entries.reason: Domain records are whatever an application stores, so no test can enumerate them. What keeps them out is that the compiler reads only its closed configuration, conventional catalog paths and the analysed TypeScript graph, and each of those is held by its own statement in this section.

entries.statement: A release MUST analyze the selected project's actual compilation graph, its syntax trees, symbols, types, and exact source spans, and MUST NOT treat a filename glob or a textual match as semantic analysis.
Where Angular analysis is enabled, a release MUST discover component templates from component metadata and parse them through a toolkit-owned adapter, and MUST NOT infer a template from a filename.

A release MUST recognize the runtime's public symbols and generated-handle metadata rather than local spelling or an import alias, and MUST follow a handle through a re-export, a constant alias, destructuring, readonly property access, a finite tuple, record, or map, a provable literal-union selection, a template local, control flow, and a generic forwarding helper that keeps the dependent handle contract.

A release MUST NOT execute application code, import a module for its side effects, call a getter, a function, or a service, evaluate an arbitrary expression, or perform a network lookup, and MUST report an unsupported unresolved use as an actionable diagnostic.
A release MUST NOT let a raw or interpolated string, an unchecked cast, an erased base value, or an unbounded index become a message identity.
A release MUST NOT execute route code and MUST NOT require a second route manifest.
A release MUST NOT treat package availability, a public export, an external entry point, or a consumer domain record as a root.

A release MUST count a reference to a generated message group as a use of every message in it, wherever the group is handed to something that could read any part of it, and MUST NOT count walking through a group to reach one message or importing it.

A release MUST follow catalog references, scope dependencies, overrides, and required assets transitively, and MUST report an unknown reference, an incompatible dependency, an ambiguity, and a prohibited cycle as errors.

A release MUST NOT delete it, fail the compilation for it, write a tombstone, or require a stale-identifier, waiver, use, or suppression ledger, and a consumer application MAY select a stricter hygiene policy.
A release MUST NOT inspect the digits inside an authored catalog value.

A release MUST NOT require a consumer application to edit it, and MUST address it through the configured package-private import base rather than a relative generated path or a compiler-only path alias.

A release MUST carry the provider, as a declaration, in the overlay that resolves those imports while an owner is analyzed, because it is the import through which an application composes the runtime, and an overlay without it reports that import unresolved and makes every application look like one composing nothing.

A release MUST place the generated root inside the Angular application whose TypeScript graph it analyzed, rather than beside an owner that merely contains that application, so it never creates a source directory that belongs to no Angular project.

A release MUST fail for an owner whose TypeScript graph it cannot discover rather than skip it, because without a graph no call site is analyzed, every message looks unused, and the run would publish an owner containing nothing and report success.
A release MUST NOT let a package source map or declaration carry a private or machine-absolute path from the machine that generated it, or an embedded copy of consumer source.

entries.section: 8. Generated roots and the translation state
entries.statement: A release writes generated output to one conventional root inside the owner and its disposable work state to another, and a consumer application MAY configure equivalents.
entries.reason: The first clause names the two default locations and the second grants a permission, so neither is a requirement a release can break. Where the roots must stay apart is the next statement.

entries.section: 8. Generated roots and the translation state
entries.statement: A release MUST keep the generated root and the work root separate from the authored catalogs, from each other, from dependencies, and from ordinary build output.

entries.section: 8. Generated roots and the translation state
entries.statement: A release MUST treat it as the consumer application's own durable project data rather than as derived output, and MUST NOT place it under a root a project ignores by default, because a checkout without it reports no stale translation rather than reporting that it cannot tell.

entries.section: 8. Generated roots and the translation state
entries.statement: A release MUST refuse a record that is present and cannot be read before it publishes any output, and MUST NOT overwrite it, because reading it as empty is that recomputation; a record that is absent is a first run.

entries.section: 8. Generated roots and the translation state
entries.statement: A release MUST write one sorted line per entry, so concurrent translation work conflicts per message rather than across the file; MUST leave the recorded source fingerprint of a stale entry unchanged, so the report survives later runs instead of clearing itself the first time it is seen; and MUST NOT keep an entry for a message or a locale that no longer exists.

A release MUST lock the owner and the affected package metadata for a mutating operation, revalidate the input fingerprints, stage the output, compare canonical bytes, and then either publish one complete accepted generation or restore the previous one.
A release MUST NOT depend on atomic replacement of a nonempty directory or on switching a symbolic link.

A release MUST accept generated output only where the marker and the applicable output identities agree before and after it is consumed, and MUST treat an absent, changing, or mismatched marker as a bounded retry or a stale-generation failure.
A release MUST NOT let a supported watch, build, or editor integration treat an intermediate filesystem event as a completed generation.
A release MUST NOT rewrite or touch a file whose bytes are unchanged, and MUST leave the completion manifest untouched where the complete plan is unchanged.
A release MUST derive stale generated files from the desired set and remove them only inside a verified toolkit-owned root, so no author maintains a list of them.

A release MUST refuse an unmarked, mismatched, mixed-ownership, linked, escaping, substituted, or ambiguous root, MUST report both identities and the command that resolves them on a mismatch, and MUST reopen and revalidate ownership, containment, casing, and link behavior before every mutation without following a link.

A release MUST reject traversal, a case-insensitive collision, a reserved name, a non-round-tripping encoding, and root aliasing, and MUST NOT write into a consumer application's build output or another tool's output tree.

A release MUST reject a property outside that set, MUST NOT accept a message or scope registry in it, and MUST NOT accept a secret, a credential, a runtime user or tenant value, or environment-mutable state.

Every settable property carries a description, and a release MUST derive the initialization command's option table from the schema rather than from a separate list, so an option the schema accepts is one the help output names and a drifted table fails the build rather than shipping an install line that is silent about a field.
A release MUST NOT support executable configuration or a second parallel configuration source, and MUST fail with the candidates where upward discovery is ambiguous.
A release MUST NOT let an application inherit or merge a neighboring configuration by directory accident.

A consumer application selects its recovery copy through a typed provider feature using ordinary generated handles, and a release MUST treat those handles as reachability roots and generate the minimal independent recovery payload from their existing catalogs, so no project maintains a marker, a raw-key list, a duplicate emergency catalog, or a parallel recovery registry.

For an owner that selects an application runtime, a release MUST report a missing or invalid recovery root as a protected correctness error in both generation and a bare check, so build wiring runs one deterministic command and never infers a production mode from environment state.

A release MUST allow an interactive initialization only on a terminal, and MUST prompt only for the source locale, the default locale, the complete supported-locale list, and any aliases before previewing the exact plan.

A noninteractive invocation supplies one option for every field the configuration accepts; a release MUST exit with the invocation failure code and print the exact complete invocation where a required one is missing, and MUST NOT perform a network lookup or guess a regional locale.

In a check that applies fixes, a release MUST apply only previewable semantics-preserving changes, and MUST NOT invent wording, change an identity, delete a message, create a suppression, or migrate topology.
Migration is the only command a release MAY allow to change established topology, configuration shape, generated layout, the import base, or toolkit-owned package metadata.
entries.reason: The statement grants migration a permission; the matching prohibitions on the other commands are separate statements in this section (the fix path, watch, and silent migration), each mapped on its own.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT change key order, flatten a block scalar, or remove quoting whose absence would change what a value means, and MUST refuse an unquoted spelling it is not certain of, because the cost of being wrong is a catalog that parses to something else.

A release MUST leave the authored catalogs in place unless their removal is requested by name, and MUST leave in place and report an import specifier or a script that has been changed since the toolkit wrote it.
Where initialization or uninstalling writes it, a release MUST keep the file's indentation and line endings, and MUST NOT write it when none of its entries changed.
A release MUST offer a dry run wherever one is meaningful, MUST put every mutating command through the output transaction, and MUST NOT prompt for a semantic choice in a noninteractive run.
A release MUST NOT let a correctness, security, compatibility, interface, ownership, or containment error be suppressed or downgraded.

Friendly behavior is the default: a bare check MUST fail only on an error, and a release MUST keep a source-freshness finding for a contract-compatible target, an unused message, and any enabled heuristic finding non-blocking.
Strict completeness, freshness, hygiene, and custom thresholds are opt-in policies, and a release MUST NOT let one weaken a protected error.

A locale with no catalog for a scope, a catalog omitting a source message, a message omitting a required plural or ordinal category, and a translation authored against a superseded source are one question asked at four granularities, and a release MUST give them the same severity under the policy.

A release MUST report what is missing against the locale that would have supplied it, once, and MUST make what the policy counts and what the runtime renders the same answer, so a project that passes the gate is a project a strict runtime renders.

Which locales the policy covers is a consumer application's declaration, made per locale in its configuration: every locale is required to be complete unless it is declared still in progress, and a release MUST keep every finding for a declared locale at advisory severity and carry the declared reason into it.

A release MUST render a human diagnostic as one line and MUST reduce text from a third-party parser or validator to its sentence before carrying it, because a code frame, a stack, or an embedded source excerpt reaches a one-line renderer as raw control characters and repeats the position the diagnostic already states.

A release MUST write only JSON to standard output and operational text to standard error, MUST NOT emit terminal escapes to a non-terminal, and MUST report machine spans as zero-based end-exclusive UTF-16 offsets and human positions as one-based.
A release MUST resolve them in that order of priority, interruption first and success last, so a run that was interrupted while already failing does not report the failure as its outcome.
A consumer application MAY narrow a suppressible advisory by code and by owner, scope, or portable path.
entries.reason: This grants the consumer a permission, which no behavior of a release can violate.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT require a reason, an assignee, a ticket, an expiry, an approval, a waiver registry, or a suppression ledger.
entries.reason: The toolkit has no suppression surface at all, so there is no field a release could start requiring without first adding one, and an absent requirement is not something a test run can observe. The closed configuration schema, held under statement 17, is where any such field would have to appear.

entries.statement: A release MUST produce byte-identical authoritative output from a clean generation with the work root deleted and the same semantic inputs.
A release MUST NOT put a timestamp, an event order, an absolute path, or a process identity in it.
Cache entries are owner-partitioned, bounded, disposable, and integrity-checked, and a release MUST ignore and recompute corrupt or incompatible state rather than fail on it.
A release MUST NOT require a daemon, an account, a service, an install hook, or a background workspace process for it.

Once a stopped watch has returned, a release MUST deliver no further event and MUST leave the watcher holding no reference that keeps the process alive; the event loop releases the operating system handle shortly after, and the host reports no event for that release.

Startup performs a full reconciliation; filesystem events are hints, so a release MUST debounce, reread content, detect a missed or overflowed event, and widen to a full bounded reconciliation where it is uncertain.

Where a cycle rereads the inputs and finds the inputs fingerprint of the cycle before it, or the refusal that cycle gave them where no fingerprint could be taken, a release MUST generate nothing and report nothing, unless something other than its inputs stopped that cycle.
The latest accepted input wins, every accepted generation goes through the output transaction, and a release MUST NOT let watch poll a remote resource or migrate topology.

entries.section: 14. Build integration and the first run
entries.statement: A consumer application uses the built runtime and toolkit packages through their public exports, and MUST NOT compile a release's repository source or deep-import a private or generated module.

entries.section: 14. Build integration and the first run
entries.statement: A release MUST supply composable commands for that and MUST NOT install a lifecycle hook, mutate a consumer application's build implicitly, or require a private Angular builder hook or a consumer compiler dependency.

entries.section: 14. Build integration and the first run
entries.statement: A release MUST make generation succeed at every point in an ordinary first run, including before a single catalog is authored, because a project with no messages is a valid project and it is the state every project is in the moment after initialization.

entries.section: 14. Build integration and the first run
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT make an install hook, a daemon, a preliminary generation pass, a commented import, a checked-in generated file, a manual registry, an edit to a generated file, or a parallel catalog manifest part of that run.

A release MUST preserve, in an export, the complete identity, the locales, the source fingerprint, the context, the MessageFormat structure, the typed inputs and functions, the rich slots and inline codes, the target state, and any toolkit data required to return without loss.
A release MUST match an import on protected complete identity alone, and MUST NOT match by wording, by similarity, by file order, or by a rewritten third-party identifier.

A release MUST validate each independently processable unit and MAY accept valid units while others stay stale or invalid, and MUST reject the whole document where the structure is ambiguous, the XML is unsafe, or the units cannot be separated.
A release MUST NOT flatten MessageFormat, corrupt an inline code, drop required metadata, invent wording, or mark content approved on its own.

A release MUST preserve inputs, selectors, slots, invariant values, URLs, and grapheme safety, rewriting only the literal parts of a parsed message, so a placeholder is never accented, padded, or elided.

Three behaviors are configured independently, and a release MUST NOT offer them as a fixed set of modes: the direction, carried by an explicit script subtag in the locale tag itself so it resolves through the same script table every locale uses; a signed length factor, where a positive value expands and a negative one contracts and absence means no length change; and boundary markers, which delimit each rendered message so a hard-coded string is visible by being untransformed.
A release MUST NOT ship a default length factor, because a generic figure is a number nobody measured.

Every pseudo-locale a release derives is accented, so a release MUST accept `XA` only on an English pseudo-locale whose script is written left to right and whose length factor is positive, MUST accept `XB` only on an English pseudo-locale whose script is written right to left, and MUST take any other pseudo-locale under one of the codes UTS #35 leaves free.

A release MUST keep the base language that of the source catalog, because the point is for a developer to see their own screens transformed, and a pseudo-locale in another language tests translation coverage instead.
A release MUST NOT introduce a private-use subtag for this.

A release MUST take the request on the build command rather than from the environment, so one configuration serves the development build that wants pseudo-locales and the production build that must not contain them, and an environment variable set once on a build runner cannot reach the production build.
A release MUST NOT run it in the runtime and MUST NOT ship it from a runtime entry point, so excluding a pseudo-locale from a production build is an absence rather than a guard.

The generated configuration lists the pseudo-locales a build generated, and a runtime MUST refuse a list that names a locale the build does not have, names one twice, names one without a script, or names one whose region claims a language or a direction it does not have; the length factor is not in the generated configuration, so only the toolkit holds `XA` to it.
A release MUST NOT offer a regex-only replacement as a correctness path.
entries.reason: The command line offers no text-replacement command, and renames go through resolved identities; a command a release does not offer is an absence no test run can observe.

entries.statement: It is generated review evidence, and a release MUST NOT turn it into a maintained ledger.
entries.reason: The semantic diff is computed on request and written nowhere, so there is no file for a release to start maintaining; whether a future change turns it into one is a design judgment rather than a behavior a test observes.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT require a tombstone, a retired-identifier registry, a waiver, an alias, or a non-reuse ledger.
entries.reason: No such record exists in the configuration schema or the catalog format, both of which are closed, so requiring one would first mean adding it; the absence of a requirement is not something a test run can observe.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT let installation, import, generation, or watch migrate an authored file silently.

A release MUST report typed product-neutral diagnostics for authoring, compilation, validation and admission, catalog loading, fallback and recovery, transitions, formatting, caching, server rendering and hydration, and integrations.

A release MUST NOT let a diagnostic turn a systemic failure into a silent success: rendering a source-locale message where a translation is missing is correct behavior and a reported one, and a catalog that failed to load is not the same event as a message that was never translated.
A release MUST NOT make a diagnostic's meaning depend on its wording, because the wording is not a compatibility surface and the code is.

A release MUST bound the summary, the path, and the number of diagnostics one operation produces, and MUST refuse or replace a control character, a directional override, or an isolate inside diagnostic text, because a diagnostic is printed to a terminal and read by a machine and neither should be steerable by the input that produced it.

A release MUST report both the value it received and the position it received it in, so a diagnostic is actionable without a second run to locate it, and MUST NOT report the value where doing so would breach section 5.
The outcome class is what a consumer application branches on, and a release MUST keep its three cases apart.

A release MUST attach a caught underlying error to the raised error's cause rather than copying it into the diagnostic, so a stack trace, a filesystem path, and whatever a consumer application's own code threw reach a developer without passing through a contract that must stay free of them.

A release MUST NOT reassign a code, and MUST NOT treat human wording, a sampling hint, or an undocumented debug detail as one, because a consumer application that keys an alert on a code should not have to re-read a sentence after an upgrade.

A release MUST derive that reference from the declaration of the codes themselves rather than maintaining a second list, because a hand-kept list is a second source that drifts on the first commit that adds a code, and the entry nobody remembers to write is the one nothing reports.

entries.section: 5. What a diagnostic may not carry
entries.statement: A release MUST exclude from a diagnostic and from an event: translated text and source or catalog bodies; message parameters and rich-slot payloads; user content; credentials, tokens, cookies, private headers, and other secrets; machine-absolute paths and user or host identity; and unsafe untrusted input text.

entries.section: 5. What a diagnostic may not carry
entries.statement: A release MUST NOT let an ordinary verbosity setting enable content capture, because a flag that turns logging up is set by people who are debugging and read by systems that retain what they are given.
entries.reason: Neither package has a verbosity, debug or log-level setting (a search of every packages/*/src for verbose, verbosity, logLevel and --debug finds none), so there is no setting whose effect a check could withdraw. The content exclusion that such a setting would have to bypass is proven under statement 59.

entries.section: 5. What a diagnostic may not carry
entries.statement: A release MUST make the reason a diagnostic carries a closed set rather than free text, so that whatever was caught, nothing of it can be copied into the diagnostic; and MUST truncate an identifier that reaches a diagnostic to a bounded length and replace any control character in it, so an identity a consumer application supplied cannot rewrite the line it appears in.
A release MAY expose narrow optional sinks for logs, metrics, traces, development inspection, and tests.
entries.reason: This permits sinks and requires none, so no release behavior can violate it.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT contain a telemetry transport, an account, an endpoint, a background upload, an analytics collector, or a vendor library, so adopting a release adds no service to a deployment diagram.

With no sink configured, a release MUST perform no observability work at all: no network request, no persistent storage, and no event construction, so an application that wants none pays nothing for the capability.
Product analytics and business events stay outside a release, and a release MUST NOT emit one.
entries.reason: Whether an event is product analytics is a judgment about its purpose, which no program can make. The event vocabulary is a closed set of operational codes in each package, and any code added to it arrives as a change to the closed-union list that someone reads.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT put anything else in one.

A release MUST report work that was cancelled, superseded, or unavailable as itself rather than as a failure, and MUST report work that belonged elsewhere as redirected: a locale change under a locale-specific origin policy is a document navigation, so reporting success would claim a transition that never ran, and reporting failure would claim a defect where the outcome was correct.

A release MUST report each entry it evicts as succeeded, with the entry's provider, scope, and locale and the number of entries it still holds; a bound it cannot keep because every entry over it is pinned as unavailable, with the number it holds; and a transferred catalog it refuses to admit as failed, with the reason `catalog-admission-failed`.

A release MUST NOT let a sink change locale resolution, catalog loading or admission, formatting, a commit, a security decision, fallback, or the request lifecycle, and MUST NOT let a sink that throws escape into a server render or leave localization state changed.

A release MUST bound every field before it emits: an identifier beyond its length bound or carrying a control character is dropped rather than truncated into something that looks like an identity, and a count or a duration outside its range is dropped rather than emitted as a number nothing measured.

A release MUST deduplicate equivalent repeated failures within a bounded window and MUST bound the set of failure identities it remembers, discarding the oldest first, so a broken catalog, a retry loop, a missing message, or a slow sink cannot produce unbounded memory or an event storm.
A release MUST verify every capability it ships, in proportion to its correctness, security, compatibility, accessibility, performance, and regression risk.
A release MUST NOT substitute a certificate, an evidence ledger, a named owner, or a test count for evidence that the behavior holds, because none of those changes when the behavior does.
entries.reason: This rules out kinds of record as a basis for a claim. A program can check that evidence exists and was produced by a passing check, which the matrix does, but it cannot tell whether someone presented a document or a count in its place.

entries.statement: A release MUST exercise a shipped capability whether or not any consumer application currently enables it.
A release MUST own the fixtures that prove its behavior, and MUST NOT treat a consumer application's own testing as closing a row of that evidence.
A consumer application corroborates the paths it genuinely enables, on the stack it genuinely runs, and a release MUST NOT read that corroboration as wider than the stack it was taken on.
entries.reason: No result from a consumer application's own suite enters a release's gate, so there is no reading of it for a program to check. The rule governs how people interpret a report from outside the release.

entries.statement: A release MUST keep fixtures that select the minimum rather than proving everything through one application that selects everything, because tree shaking, entry-point isolation, deep-import refusal, and toolkit code staying out of a browser graph are all claims about what is absent, and an application holding every capability cannot demonstrate an absence.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release MUST name the checks it deliberately does not run.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release MUST keep a matrix with every capability it ships as a row and every context it verifies in as a column, and MUST derive both from what it publishes and what its gate declares rather than from a list kept beside them, so a capability or a context added later has its row or its column on the day it lands.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release MUST refuse a claim for a capability its check never names, and MUST record nothing from a run under an injected defect.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: Every other cell MUST carry a reason, in a file the release keeps, stating why the capability cannot be exercised in that context, and the gate MUST fail on a cell with neither.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: The gate MUST also fail on a reason that covers an exercised cell or covers none, because a reason that outlives its cause hides the next gap in the same place.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release MUST map every normative statement to the checks that prove it, each one a check the gate proves able to fail as section 9 requires, or to a reason no check can prove it.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: The gate MUST fail on a statement with neither, on an entry that names a check the gate does not prove, and on an entry whose statement the documents no longer make, because an edited requirement is read against its proof before it counts as proven again.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release MAY verify direction, document language, isolation, and its live region as attributes and computed styles rather than by comparing images, because those are the properties the runtime owns and an image comparison also fails on a consumer application's unrelated redesign.
entries.reason: This grants a choice of verification method. No release can violate a permission, so there is nothing for a check to withdraw.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release SHOULD verify its parsers, canonicalizers, and formatters with generated valid input checked against a property rather than with random bytes.

entries.section: 3. Coverage, and the checks a release does not run
entries.statement: A release MUST seed a generator from a constant it carries, so a failure is reproducible rather than merely reported.
