A release MUST verify refusal as thoroughly as acceptance, and MUST cover at least: - invalid, duplicate, and malformed catalogs, and unknown functions, slots, inputs, and identities; - an artifact refused for identity, compatibility, integrity, provenance, or a resource limit; - a failed load, a cancellation, a coalesced or superseded transition, and racing transitions; - a participant that is pending, that fails, that has no representation, and that answers with a valid domain outcome; - consumer content reaching a catalog, a cache, a snapshot, transfer state, a diagnostic, or an event; - request isolation, cleanup, hydration mismatch, and transfer reuse; - a missing translation under every fallback and recovery setting; - unsafe rich content, unsafe URLs, authored bidirectional controls, and XML, YAML, and JSON attacks; - exhaustion of decompression, parsing, analysis, evaluation, caching, and diagnostics.
A release MUST verify a validator against values that are not text at all, because a parameter declared as text stops nothing at a boundary where the type is not present.

A release MUST verify its mechanisms against locales that differ in the ways those mechanisms depend on, covering at least a right to left language, plural categories beyond one and other, non-Latin digits, a script written without spaces, complex shaping, a supplying language different from the target, content whose language is unknown or deliberately fixed, and a pseudo-locale.
A release MUST take a locale's categories, endonyms, and formats from the locale data it pins rather than from the host, so an answer does not change with whichever runtime a build happens to use.
A fixture matrix verifies mechanisms, and a release MUST NOT turn one into a production locale default.
entries.reason: This is a rule about where a release's defaults come from. A default that happens to equal a fixture's locale list and one copied from it are the same value, so no program can tell the two apart; what a program can see is that no default locale set ships, which equator init already requires the application to supply.

entries.statement: Where a standard the profile pins publishes a conformance suite, a release MUST run that suite for the edition it declares, pinned by digest, and through its built packages.
A release MUST record which stage answers a case rather than reshaping the case to reach a particular one.
entries.reason: The conformance run records the stage that answered each case, but whether a case was rewritten to reach a different stage is a judgment about the case's content against the published suite, which is pinned by digest and cannot be edited without failing verify:standards-sources.

entries.statement: Where a release promises something statically, a fixture MUST fail when the promise is withdrawn.

A release MUST verify a resolved instance rather than a provider declaration wherever a consumer application is asked to replace or subclass an injectable, because a subclass inherits its base's provider and resolving it can silently construct the very implementation the subclass was written to replace.
entries.reason: This governs how a test for a replaceable injectable is written. Whether a test reads the injector's answer or trusts a provider list is visible to a reader of the test, and no withdrawal of runtime behavior tells the two kinds of test apart.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT hold an export used on evidence that disappears, such as a scratch file or a throwaway script, and MUST NOT answer the question with a count, because a count is a ceiling that new unreachable surface fits under.
A release MUST check its formatting and parsing against an authority it did not write.
A release MUST give a repaired defect the smallest durable test at the layer that owns it, and SHOULD prefer a property over a single case wherever the defect has a shape that other inputs share.
entries.reason: Which layer owns a defect and whether a test is the smallest durable one are judgments made when a fix is written. A program can see that a test exists, not that it sits at the right layer.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT rest a claim on a broad snapshot, on a duplicate of framework behavior, or on an assertion about an implementation detail.
entries.reason: Whether an assertion is about a behavior or about an implementation detail, and whether a snapshot is broad, depends on what the claim is. That is read in review of the test, and no program run can withdraw it.

entries.statement: A release MUST prove that its checks can fail, by withdrawing the behavior a check guards and requiring that check to notice.

A check that reads what a build or a repository holds rather than a behavior, such as a stage over the built packages, the standards lock, or a generated reference, is proven the same way: a release MUST plant each defect the check exists to refuse into a copy of what it reads, and MUST require the check to pass on the unchanged copy and to refuse each planted defect by name.
A release MUST NOT derive a check from the thing it checks.
entries.reason: Whether an expected value was computed through the code under test is a property of how the check was built. Two checks with the same assertions can differ only in where their expected values came from, which a reviewer reads and a program run cannot withdraw.

entries.statement: A release MUST treat an absent observation as absent rather than as agreement, so a failure of the observing mechanism cannot present itself as a clean result.
Where a check compares against a recorded baseline, a release MUST make recording that baseline a separate deliberate act, and MUST NOT let a failing run rewrite the baseline it is failing against.

A release MUST publish reproducible measurements for its runtime, its framework integration, its generated contracts, its compiler work, and its packages, and MUST measure each published entry point separately.
A release MUST assert the shape of a cost rather than an absolute duration wherever the measurement runs on a machine it does not control.
entries.reason: This decides how a cost check is written, as a ratio between its own measurements rather than a number of milliseconds. The form of a check's limit is fixed when the check is written, and withdrawing Equator's behavior does not change it.

entries.statement: A release MUST vary what the cost depends on: message, scope, provider, and locale counts; message complexity; cold and warm generation; initial and lazy catalog loading; coordinated and progressive locale switching; participant count and readiness; server rendering concurrency and hydration transfer; cache pressure; repeated failure; and adversarial input at and beyond the allowed bounds.
A release MUST impose a hard ceiling only where a safe algorithm or resistance to a denial of service requires one.
entries.reason: Whether a ceiling is needed for safety is decided when the ceiling is designed. A program can check that a ceiling holds, which the statements owning each limit map, but not why it exists.

entries.statement: Defaults SHOULD be generous, automatic, and configurable by a consumer application within ceilings the release does not allow to be bypassed.
entries.reason: Whether a default is generous is a judgment against how the library is used. That a configured value above a ceiling is refused is a property of each limit, and is proven under the statement that owns that limit.

entries.statement: A release MUST establish a numeric threshold by measurement and record it in the document that owns it, and MUST NOT present a guessed number as a timeless one.
entries.reason: How a number was arrived at is a fact about the work that produced it. The number itself is the same whether it was measured or guessed, so no program can tell the two apart.

entries.statement: Where the property under test is a cost, a release MUST verify it by a count the machine cannot change, and MUST NOT keep a recorded timing figure as the threshold a later run is compared against.
A release MUST size one so that reaching it means the test was never going to finish, and MUST NOT use one as a performance budget.
entries.reason: A timeout's purpose is decided when it is sized. The same number can be a hang detector for one test and a budget for another, and only the measurement it was sized from says which.

entries.statement: A release MUST NOT require a consumer application to adopt a capability, invent a feature, or run a check merely to widen a release's own evidence.
entries.reason: The rule limits what a release may ask of an application outside it. Nothing a consumer application runs feeds the gate, so there is no requirement a program could find in a build and withdraw.

entries.statement: A release MUST supply the commands, fixtures, and testing surface a consumer application needs to verify its own use of a release, and MUST NOT attempt to size a consumer application's host.

A release MUST NOT require a second record of anything it derives: no locale registry beside the declaration, no alias for a relation the locked data already states, no digest, version, or revision field in an authored file, and no ledger of what changed.
